  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from 0 to 120, default 3

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Right-clicking again on the PDF within this time (3 second default) will prevent the Auto-update from running.

Explanation:

When Auto-update is on in the PDF Preview window, a right-click adjustment starts a new print after this many seconds. If you right-click again within this time, PTXprint waits, so you can make several adjustments before it prints. Increase it if you need more time between adjustments.

Shrink Text Step Value (%)

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from 1 to 5, default 1

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Step Value to shrink text using right-click context menu adjustment.

Explanation:

How many percent each "shrink text" step from the right-click menu in the PDF Preview window makes a paragraph smaller.

Minimum Text Shrink (%)

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from 85 to 100, default 95

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Limit how much text can shrink to using right-click context menu adjustment.

Explanation:

The smallest size (in percent of normal) that a paragraph can be shrunk to with the right-click menu. 95 means at most 5% smaller. The page filler also uses this limit. Shrinking too much makes text look crowded.

Expand Text Step Value (%)

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from 1 to 5, default 1

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Step Value to expand text using right-click context menu adjustment.

Explanation:

How many percent each "expand text" step from the right-click menu makes a paragraph larger.

Maximum Text Expand (%)

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from 100 to 115, default 105

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Limit how much text can expand to using right-click context menu adjustment.

Explanation:

The largest size (in percent of normal) that a paragraph can be expanded to with the right-click menu. 105 means at most 5% larger.

Bad Space minimum width (em)

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from 0 to 10, default 1.3

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Minimum width for a bad space. 0 says to calculate for the 20 worst spaces in the doc

Explanation:

Layout Analysis in the PDF Preview window marks word spaces wider than this, in em (the size of the font). With 0, PTXprint finds the 20 widest spaces in the document instead. A lower value marks more spaces.

Bad intercharacter space minimum width (em)

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from 0 to 1, default 0.3

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Minimum width for a bad inter character space.

Explanation:

Layout Analysis marks spaces between letters wider than this, in em. It is only used when letter spacing is turned on (Between Letters on the Fonts+Script tab).

Precise collisions

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Only show precise collisions between glyphs rather than overlapping bounding boxes - slow

Explanation:

When ticked, collision checking looks at the real shapes of the letters, not just the boxes around them. It finds fewer false collisions but is slow.

Collision Detection Padding (pt)

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from -1 to 5, default 0.5

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Minimum space between bounding boxes of glyphs before a collision is flagged.

Explanation:

How close (in points) the boxes around letters on different lines can come before Layout Analysis reports a collision. A larger value reports more possible collisions.

River Detection Threshold (em)

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from 1 to 1000, default 3

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

The sum of all the widths in the river must be above this for the river to be detected

Explanation:

A river is a line of white space running down through several lines of text. A river is reported only when the widths of all its spaces add up to more than this, in em. Increase it to report only the worst rivers.

River Detection minimum required maximum width (em)

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from 0.1 to 5, default 1

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Minimum width required for the widest part of the river

Explanation:

A river is reported only if its widest space is at least this wide (in em).

River Detection minimum width (em)

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from 0.1 to 5, default 0.5

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Minimum width of any space in a river for it to be included

Explanation:

A space must be at least this wide (in em) to be counted as part of a river.

River Detection maximum line leading (em)

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from 0 to 5, default 0.4

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Any lines separated by a gap greater than this will be considered not to be in the same river

Explanation:

Spaces on lines that are further apart than this (in em) are not counted as one river.

River Detection minimum overlap (em)

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from -5 to 5, default 0.4

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Minimum overlap in ems required for two spaces above each other to be considered part of the same river

Explanation:

Two spaces on lines above each other must overlap by at least this much (in em) to belong to the same river.

Advanced tab › Other tab › Automatic Page Filler

Time limit for the whole job (minutes)

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Automatic Page Filler
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from 0 to 1000, default 180

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

The page filler works on all the books together. When this time is reached, the page filler stops. A book that is not finished keeps the pages that are already filled. Usually this affects only the longest book.
Higher: more time to find a good layout for every page.

Explanation:

The longest time in minutes that the page filler works on the whole job. When the time is up, it stops. Pages it has already filled are kept. 0 means no time limit. Increase it for a long Bible if the longest book does not finish.

Earlier pages to retry

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Automatic Page Filler
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from 0 to 10, default 4

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

If the page filler cannot fill a page, it backtracks to the page before and tries a different layout there. This is the largest number of pages it can backtrack.
Higher: fewer failed pages, but much slower.
Lower: faster, but more pages may fail. 0 = never backtrack (fastest).
Affects: Speed.

Explanation:

When the page filler cannot fill a page, it can go back to earlier pages and try a different layout there. This is how many pages it may go back. Higher values fail on fewer pages but are much slower.

Paragraphs to adjust on each page

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Automatic Page Filler
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from 1 to 10, default 6

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

The largest number of paragraphs on one page that the page filler may stretch or shrink. Each poetry line (\q1, \q2 …) counts as one paragraph. Each extra paragraph doubles the number of layouts the page filler tries.
Higher: more ways to fill each page, so fewer failed pages, but each page takes longer.
Lower: faster, but more pages may fail.
Affects: Speed.

Explanation:

How many paragraphs on one page the page filler may stretch or shrink. Each poetry line counts as a paragraph. Each extra paragraph doubles the work, so keep this low unless many pages fail.

Widest word space allowed (× text size)

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Automatic Page Filler
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from 0 to 10, default 1

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

When the page filler stretches a paragraph, the average space between words must not be wider than this. 1.0 = as wide as the text size. A normal word space is about 0.3 to 0.5.
Higher: easier to fill pages, but the text can look too spread out.
Lower: tighter, better-looking text, but pages are harder to fill and take longer.
Affects: Quality and Speed.

Explanation:

The widest average word space the page filler allows when it stretches a paragraph, as a part of the text size. A normal word space is about 0.3 to 0.5. Lower values look better, but more pages may fail and filling takes longer.

Keep paragraphs close to normal width

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Automatic Page Filler
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from 0 to 10, default 1

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

The page filler prefers small changes to a paragraph over big changes. This setting controls how strong that preference is. Higher: the page filler tries small changes first, so the text looks more even.
Lower: the page filler accepts big changes more easily.
Affects: Quality.

Explanation:

How strongly the page filler prefers small changes to paragraphs over large ones. Higher values give more even text.

Penalise shrink or stretch

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Automatic Page Filler
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from -5 to 5, default 1

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Tells the page filler whether to shrink paragraphs or stretch them when both are possible.
Positive numbers: penalise stretching (so the text prefers to shrink more).
Negative numbers: penalise shrinking. (so the text prefers to stretch more).
0: no preference.
A bigger number (+ or −) means a higher penalty.
Affects: Quality.

Explanation:

Whether the page filler prefers to shrink or to stretch paragraphs when both would work. Positive values prefer shrinking. Negative values prefer stretching. 0 has no preference.

Keep neighbouring paragraphs alike

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Automatic Page Filler
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from 0 to 20, default 3

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

The page filler compares each paragraph with the paragraph before it. It tries to avoid a very stretched paragraph next to a very shrunk one.
Higher: neighbouring paragraphs look more alike, so the page looks more even.
Lower: neighbouring paragraphs can look more different.
Affects: Quality.

Explanation:

How strongly the page filler avoids a very stretched paragraph next to a very shrunk one. Higher values give a more even page.

Advanced tab › Other tab › Other Miscellaneous Settings

Use \toc3 for Tab Text

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Other Miscellaneous Settings
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Use \toc3 for tab text if no \zthumbtab

Explanation:

When ticked (the default), the thumb tab text of a book comes from its \toc3 (short book name), if the book has no \zthumbtab marker. Thumb tabs are set on the Tabs+Borders tab.

Tilde is No Break Space

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Other Miscellaneous Settings
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Treat ~ as non breaking space

Explanation:

When ticked (the default), a tilde (~) in the text prints as a non-breaking space. A non-breaking space looks like a normal space, but the line never breaks there. Untick it only if your text needs to print a real tilde character.

Remove \ref ... \ref* links

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Other Miscellaneous Settings
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

USFM 3.2 allows additional reference links to be inserted as part of \xt ... \xt* markup. This frequently appear in DBL text bundles, but are unhandled by PTXprint. Allow these to be removed from the USFM prior to typesetting.

Explanation:

Text from the Digital Bible Library (DBL) often has extra \ref links inside cross-references. PTXprint cannot use them. When ticked (the default), they are removed before typesetting, and only their visible text is kept.

End decoration skip

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Other Miscellaneous Settings
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from -100 to 100, default 16

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

The gap between the end of the book and the book-end decoration

Explanation:

The space (in points) between the end of the book text and the end-of-book decoration. The decoration is turned on in Ornamental Decorations on the Tabs+Borders tab. Use negative values to move the decoration up.

Thumbtab rotated adjustment

  • Where: Advanced tab › Other tab › Other Miscellaneous Settings
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from -10 to 50, default -2

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Shift thumbtab text

Explanation:

Moves the text on rotated thumb tabs (in points) so that it sits in the middle of the tab. Change it if the tab text looks off-centre. Thumb tabs and Rotate Tabs are on the Tabs+Borders tab.

View+Edit tab

What this tab is for

The View+Edit tab lets you look at the files that PTXprint uses and creates. For two of these files you can also make changes here: the front matter (the pages before the Scripture text, such as the title page and the table of contents) and the Adj List (the list of paragraph adjustments).

Come here when you want to:

  • create or change the front matter (title page, copyright page, contents page, preface);
  • make a paragraph one line longer or shorter so that a page fits better;
  • look at the text exactly as PTXprint sent it to the typesetting program;
  • look at the log of the last print run when something went wrong.

This tab is only shown in the Default and Full views. In the Basic view you cannot see it, but PTXprint still uses the front matter and Adj List that you made before.

The sub-tabs: which files you may edit

The tab has several small tabs (sub-tabs) along the top. Each one shows one file.

Sub-tab What it shows Can you edit it here?
Front Matter The front matter for this configuration (title page, copyright page, contents, and so on). Yes. This is the main place to edit front matter.
Adj List A table of paragraph adjustments for the Book in Focus. Yes. You can change values in the table.
Final SFM The text of one book after PTXprint has applied all its changes, as it was sent to the typesetter. No – look only. It is created again each time you print.
.tex file The control file that PTXprint wrote for the last print run. No – look only.
XeTeX Log The log (report) of the last print run. No – look only.
Settings (up to three) Other settings files that you chose to open from the Advanced tab. Advanced users only – see the Advanced tab chapter.

Important: Changes to the Scripture text itself must be made in Paratext. Do not try to correct the text on the Final SFM sub-tab. That file is replaced every time you print.

The .tex file and XeTeX Log sub-tabs are useful when you ask for help. A supporter may ask you to look for an error message in the XeTeX Log. You do not need to understand these files to use PTXprint.

Very long log files are cut short on the screen. Click View/Edit... to see the whole file in your computer's text editor.

The buttons at the top of the tab

The row of buttons at the top changes with the sub-tab that is open. Some buttons are greyed out on sub-tabs where they do not apply.

  • Refresh reloads the file from the disk. Any changes you have not saved are lost.
  • Book in Focus chooses which book is shown. It is only active on the Adj List and Final SFM sub-tabs.
  • Generate creates new content for the open sub-tab (see below).
  • View/Edit... opens the file in your computer's own text editor. On the look-only sub-tabs the button is called View Only....
  • Edit Variables... (only on the Front Matter sub-tab) takes you to the table of variables on the Peripherals tab.
  • The information button (only active on the Front Matter sub-tab) shows a list of special codes when you hold the mouse over it.
  • Autosave decides whether changes are saved without asking.
  • The slider changes the size of the text in the editing area.

Saving your changes

When you change the text on an editable sub-tab, the name of the sub-tab turns red. This means there are unsaved changes. PTXprint saves the changes:

  • when you click somewhere outside the text area (without asking if Autosave is ticked, or after asking you if it is not ticked);
  • when you click Print while an editable sub-tab is open.

If you do not want your changes, click Refresh (or press F5) before you click elsewhere.

If the configuration is locked (see the Basic tab), you cannot generate or save front matter, and Autosave is turned off.

The Generate button

Generate does a different job on each sub-tab:

  • Front Matter – opens the Generate Front Matter dialog, so you can start the front matter from a template.
  • Adj List – makes a new adjustment list for the books you are printing (see The Adj List below).
  • Final SFM – makes the Final SFM file again for the Book in Focus, so you can look at it.

On the other sub-tabs Generate is greyed out.

The Generate Front Matter dialog

This dialog appears when you click Generate on the Front Matter sub-tab. You choose one of four starting points:

  • BASIC – a title page, a page with copyright and licence information, and a table of contents. This is a good start for most projects.
  • ADVANCED – more sections (title page, publication data, foreword, preface, table of contents, alphabetical contents). It contains sample English text. You must change the text into your language, or delete the sections you do not want.
  • DIGLOT – a fuller template for diglot or polyglot publications (two or more languages). It is only available when Diglot is turned on for this configuration. Delete the sections you do not need.
  • PARATEXT – copies the FRT (front matter) book from your Paratext project. It is greyed out if the project has no FRT book. After the copy, changes in Paratext are not copied here automatically. Generate again if you want the new Paratext version.

Warning: When you click OK, the new template replaces all of the front matter that is there now. Your earlier changes are lost. If you have worked on your front matter, click Cancel.

After you click OK, PTXprint also looks for variables (\zvar|...\* codes) in the new front matter and adds any new ones to the variables table on the Peripherals tab.

The front matter and its special codes (advanced)

The front matter uses USFM markers, the same kind of markers that Paratext uses (for example \mt1 for a main title and \pc for a centred paragraph). PTXprint also understands some extra codes. These start with \z and are often called z-codes. Hold the mouse over the information button to see a short list.

Each configuration has its own front matter. If you make a new configuration, check its front matter too.

Sections (periph)

The front matter is divided into sections. Each section starts with a line such as:

\periph Title Page|id="title"

Each section normally starts on a new page.

Text from other settings

  • \zcopyright – the copyright statement from the Basic tab.
  • \zlicense – the licence statement from the Basic tab. (Type it with an s.)
  • \zimagecopyrights – a list of the pictures used, with their pages and copyright credits. You can add a language code at the end, for example \zimagecopyrightsfr for French. The list is only correct after you have printed twice, because PTXprint first needs to find out on which page each picture is.

Put these codes after a paragraph marker, for example: \pc \zcopyright

Variables

\zvar|maintitle\* is a variable: a place-holder for a piece of text. When you print, PTXprint replaces it with the value from the variables table on the Peripherals tab. You can make up your own names, for example \zvar|printedby\*. The values are saved with the configuration, so two configurations can use the same front matter with different titles.

\zvar|toctitle\* is special. It uses the text in the Table of contents title box on the Peripherals tab.

Space and blank lines

  • \zbl|3\* – inserts 3 blank lines.
  • \zgap|1.5in\* – inserts a space of the given height (for example 1.5in, 20mm, 30pt).

Page numbers

  • \nopagenums – do not print page numbers from here on.
  • \dopagenums – print page numbers again.
  • \resetpagenums -1 – start the page numbers again. A negative number gives Roman numerals (i, ii, iii...).

Table of contents

\ztoc|main\* puts the table of contents here. Instead of main you can use: pre (books before the Scripture text), ot (Old Testament only), heb (Old Testament in Hebrew order), dc (Deuterocanon only), nt (New Testament only), post (books after Revelation, such as a glossary), or sorta, sortb, sortc (alphabetical lists sorted by \toc1, \toc2 or \toc3). The table of contents must also be turned on with Table of Contents on the Peripherals tab.

Code Snippets buttons

On the Front Matter sub-tab, buttons under Code Snippets list ready-made codes in groups (for example Periph+Var, Insert, ISBN+QR, Contents, Pages, Diglot). Put the cursor where you want the code. Click a group button, then choose an item. PTXprint inserts the code at the cursor. Hold the mouse over an item to see what it does. The Settings sub-tabs have their own snippet buttons for the type of file that is open.

Keyboard shortcuts in the front matter editor

  • Ctrl+0 or Ctrl+comma – turn the current line into a comment (\rem), or back again.
  • Ctrl+D – copy (duplicate) the current line.
  • Ctrl+L – delete the current line.
  • Ctrl+Up / Ctrl+Down – move the current line up or down.
  • Ctrl+minus / Ctrl+equals – make the text in the editor smaller or larger.
  • Alt+X – show the Unicode values of the selected characters in the status bar.

The Adj List (adjustment list)

PTXprint fills each page with lines of text. Sometimes a page ends badly: for example, one line of a paragraph is alone at the top of the next page, or the two columns do not end at the same height. You can often fix this by asking PTXprint to set one paragraph a little tighter (so it uses one line less) or a little looser (so it uses one line more).

The Adj List is the list of these requests. Each row is one paragraph. The columns are:

  • Book and C.V – the book and the chapter and verse where the paragraph is.
  • Para – which paragraph: 1 is the paragraph that contains the verse, 2 is the next one, and so on. This lets you adjust, for example, the paragraph after a heading.
  • Stretch – the change. +1 asks for one line more, -1 for one line less. After Generate, you will also see values such as +0, -0 or +-0. These mean "no change yet", and they show whether the paragraph can grow (+) or shrink (-).
  • Marker – the paragraph marker (for example p or q1).
  • Expand – how much the letters are spread out or squeezed, in percent. 100 is normal.
  • Parameters and Comment – extra information.

Click a cell to change its value. To delete rows, select them and press the Delete key, or right-click and choose Delete Row(s).

For a diglot, the book code has an L or R after it (for example MATL and MATR), to say which side the paragraph is on.

Generate on the Adj List sub-tab prints the books three times in the background (once normal, once tight, once loose). From this it learns which paragraphs can shrink or grow. This can take some time. If an Adj List already exists, PTXprint asks if you want to replace it (Yes), merge the new information into it (No – the safe choice), or do nothing (Cancel).

In most cases it is easier to make adjustments from the PDF Preview window. There you can right-click a paragraph and choose to shrink or expand it. PTXprint writes those changes into this same Adj List.

Do paragraph adjustments last. Any change to fonts, margins, pictures or other layout settings moves the text, and your adjustments may then be wrong.

Common tasks

Create front matter for the first time

  1. Go to the Peripherals tab and tick Local Front Matter. If there is no front matter yet, PTXprint makes a BASIC one for you.
  2. Go to the View+Edit tab and click the Front Matter sub-tab.
  3. If you want a different template, click Generate, choose BASIC, ADVANCED, DIGLOT or PARATEXT, and click OK.
  4. Click Edit Variables... and type the values (title, subtitle and so on) in the Value column.
  5. Click Print. If the front matter has a table of contents or picture credits, click Print a second time.

Change the text on the title page

  1. On the View+Edit tab, click the Front Matter sub-tab.
  2. If the line says \mt1 \zvar|maintitle\*, the title comes from a variable. Click Edit Variables... and change the value of maintitle.
  3. If the line contains normal text, change the text directly in the editor.
  4. Click outside the text area to save, then click Print.

Add a copyright page with picture credits

  1. Open the Front Matter sub-tab.

  2. Put the cursor where the copyright information should go.

  3. Type these lines (or use the Insert snippet button):

     \pc \zcopyright
 \pc \zlicense
 \pc \zimagecopyrights

  4. Click Print twice.

Make a paragraph one line shorter or longer

  1. Finish all other layout settings first.
  2. Open the PDF in the PDF Preview window and right-click the paragraph to shrink or expand it. This is the easiest way.
  3. Or: on the View+Edit tab, click the Adj List sub-tab, choose the Book in Focus, find the paragraph and type -1 or +1 in the Stretch column.
  4. Click Print and check the result.

See what text PTXprint actually typeset

  1. Click Print once, so the file exists.
  2. On the View+Edit tab, click the Final SFM sub-tab.
  3. Choose the book in Book in Focus.
  4. Read the text. Do not edit it – make corrections in Paratext instead.

Look at the log after a failed print

  1. Click the XeTeX Log sub-tab.
  2. Scroll to the end. Error messages usually start with !.
  3. If the log is cut short, click View Only... to open the whole file.

Common problems

My changes to the front matter disappeared. You probably clicked Generate and then OK. This replaces the whole front matter. Or you clicked Refresh, or answered "No" when PTXprint asked "Save changes?". There is no undo. In future, keep a copy of important text before you generate a new template.

The front matter does not appear in the PDF. Local Front Matter on the Peripherals tab must be ticked.

A variable prints as "". PTXprint found the variable in the front matter but nobody has given it a value. Go to the Peripherals tab and type a value for it in the variables table.

The licence statement does not print. Check that the code is spelled \zlicense (with an s).

The table of contents or the picture credits are empty or wrong. PTXprint needs a first print run to find the page numbers. Click Print again.

The View+Edit tab is missing. You are using the Basic or Minimal view. Change the view level to Default or Full in the main menu.

The Generate button is greyed out. It does not work on the .tex file, XeTeX Log and Settings sub-tabs. On the Front Matter sub-tab, it is also greyed out when the configuration is locked.

"The Book in focus is not within scope". You clicked Generate on the Adj List sub-tab, but the Book in Focus is not in the list of books to print. Choose a book that you are printing, or add the book on the Basic tab.

Paragraph adjustments no longer do what I expected. The layout has changed since you made them (for example a new font size or new pictures). Check the adjustments again, or generate a new Adj List.

Settings reference: View+Edit tab

Every control in this part of PTXprint is listed below, grouped by where it appears.

Generate Front Matter (dialog)

OK

  • Where: Generate Front Matter (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • View level: Default and Full views

Explanation:

Replaces the current front matter with the template you chose. Anything you typed in the front matter before is lost, so only click this if you really want to start again.

Cancel

  • Where: Generate Front Matter (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • View level: Default and Full views

Explanation:

Closes the dialog and keeps your front matter as it is. Click this if you are not sure.

Generate Front Matter (dialog) › Generate Front Matter

BASIC: Front matter contains just a few essentials with publication information

  • Where: Generate Front Matter (dialog) › Generate Front Matter
  • Type: Radio button
  • Description: Generate front matter: BASIC (just the essentials)
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

This option will create a simple verso page containing essential copyright and licensing information followed by a table of contents.

Explanation:

The simplest template: a title page, a publication data page (copyright, licence and picture credits) and a table of contents. The titles come from variables such as maintitle and subtitle, so you only need to fill in the variables table on the Peripherals tab. A good choice for most first-time users.

ADVANCED: template contains several sections (some of which require editing before use)

  • Where: Generate Front Matter (dialog) › Generate Front Matter
  • Type: Radio button
  • Description: Generate front matter: ADVANCED (requires editing)
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

This option will create an extensive template with multiple sections (each of which will start on a new page in the final publication). You will need to edit the sample text provided so that it communicates in the required language(s). You can also remove unwanted sections if they are inappropriate for this publication. Note: In order to make this template generic for several different publications in this project, you are encouraged to use \zvar|variables\* which will be replaced with publication-specific info when printed. For example:
\mt1 \zvar|maintitle\*
\mt2 \zvar|subtitle\*
\pc \zvar|maintitlefr\*
\pc \zvar|subtitlefr\*
\pc \zvar|languagename\*
\pc \zvar|copiesprinted\*

Explanation:

A longer template with title page, publication data, foreword, preface, table of contents and an alphabetical contents list. The foreword and preface contain sample English text that you must replace or delete. It also uses more variables (for example languagename, copiesprinted, printedby), which you fill in on the Peripherals tab.

Include sections for a separate cover page

  • Where: Generate Front Matter (dialog) › Generate Front Matter
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • Description: Generate front matter: Include sections for cover page
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

(Not yet implemented) Enable this option if you want to include the following sections (used for creating a cover page):
\periph Cover - detailing text and optional picture
\periph Spine - text for the spine of the cover

Explanation:

This option does not do anything yet in the current version, whether it is ticked or not. To make a cover, use Create Cover Page and the Cover Wizard... on the Peripherals tab instead.

DIGLOT: template for a Diglot or Polyglot publication (deliberately fuller — delete sections you do not need)

  • Where: Generate Front Matter (dialog) › Generate Front Matter
  • Type: Radio button
  • Description: Generate front matter: DIGLOT (for Diglot/Polyglot publications)
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

This option creates a DIGLOT / POLYGLOT front matter template designed for publications with two (or more) languages or scripts. It is deliberately more complete than the BASIC and ADVANCED templates because diglots are inherently complex: two (or more) texts, often two contents lists, two prefaces, sometimes two scripts and two writing directions. Delete the sections you do not need.

Like the ADVANCED template it uses \zvar|variables\* and
\zglot|L\* / \zglot|R\* markers for column-specific content, so it requires editing before use and is NOT suitable for use inside Paratext without prior modification.

If this option is disabled, the Diglot setting is not enabled for this configuration.

Explanation:

A template for publications with two or more languages. It includes sections for both languages (for example two prefaces taken from each side's INT book) and also cover sections. It is greyed out unless Diglot is turned on for this configuration. Expect to delete several sections you do not need.

PARATEXT: Make a copy of the Project's FRT book (which may be edited to make use of \zvar|variables\*)

  • Where: Generate Front Matter (dialog) › Generate Front Matter
  • Type: Radio button
  • Description: Generate front matter: PARATEXT (make a local copy)
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

This option will create a COPY of the Paratext project's FRT book to be used exclusively by PTXprint. You can edit the front matter to make use of PTXprint-specific
\zvar|variables\* but note that none of these edits will be reflected in Paratext. In addition, if you edit the FRT book in Paratext, those changes will not be reflected here until you regenerate this (local) Front Matter.

If option is disabled, it is due to not having a FRT book in the Paratext project (so there is nothing to import).

Explanation:

Copies the FRT book from the Paratext project into PTXprint's own front matter. After that, the two are separate: edits in Paratext do not appear here, and edits here do not go back to Paratext. Use this if your team already keeps good front matter in Paratext. It is greyed out if the project has no FRT book.

Generate

This button will (re-)generate content for Front Matter, AdjList(s) and Final SFM.

View/Edit...

Use the following codes to include special text in front matter:

\nopagenums - turn OFF page numbers

post – books that occur after REV (GLO, BAK, TDX, NDX, XXA-G)

In addition to the above-mentioned codes, you may specify your own config-specific \zvar|variables\* as place-holders. Click on 'Edit Variables...' to assign values to these variables on the Peripherals tab. For example:

An information button. Hold the mouse over it to see a short list of the special codes you can type in the front matter. It is only active on the Front Matter sub-tab. See the section "The front matter and its special codes" in this chapter for a fuller explanation.

Ctrl-Minus - shrink text size
Ctrl-Plus - grow text size

Adj List

  • Where: View+Edit tab
  • Type: Label
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

To balance columns of text on a page it is possible to specify paragraphs adjustments (shrink or expand):

A Paragraph Adjust List needs to be in this format:
MRK 2.7 +1 (i.e. expand the para at Mark 2.7 by one line) MRK 3.20 -1 (i.e. shrink the para at Mark 3:20 by one line) %MARK 4.14 +1 (ignore this line - treat it as a comment) MRK 5.8 +2 (i.e. expand the para at Mark 5.8 by two lines) MRK 6.23 +1[2] (expand the paragraph AFTER the paragraph
which contains MRK 6.23 e.g. a heading.)

Diglot AdjList also need R or L to be specified after the book code and it is important that L comes before R for the same verse. MATL 3.4 +1 MATR 3.4 -1 MATR 3.11 +2

Keyboard Shortcuts:
Ctrl-1 - makes the current line +1
Ctrl-2 - makes the 2nd para of current line +1[2]
... etc ...
Ctrl-9 - makes the 9th para of current line +1[9]

Ctrl-I - shrink current line -1
Ctrl-Grave - ` same as above

Ctrl-0 - % Comment (or uncomment) the line [it toggles]
Ctrl-Comma - same as above

Ctrl-D - Duplicate the current line
Ctlr-L - deLete the current line
Ctrl-Up - move the current line up one line
Ctrl-Down - move the current line down one line

Note that adjusting paragraphs needs to be done right at the end when all other settings have been finalized. Otherwise you are likely to have to re-do it all again.

Explanation:

The name of the Adj List sub-tab. The table on this sub-tab shows one row per paragraph for the Book in Focus. Type +1 or -1 in the Stretch column to make a paragraph one line longer or shorter. See "The Adj List (adjustment list)" in this chapter for the meaning of each column.

Peripherals tab (front and back matter)

What this tab is for

The Peripherals tab controls everything that is printed around the Scripture text:

  • the front matter – the pages before the Scripture text, such as the title page, the copyright page and the table of contents;
  • the back matter – pages after the Scripture text, such as maps and the colophon;
  • a cover for the book;
  • ready-made PDF files that you want to add at the front or at the back.

Come here when you want a title page, a table of contents, a copyright statement, maps or a cover. The words on these pages are written in the front matter. You edit the front matter on the View+Edit tab. The special codes that you can use there (\zcopyright, \ztoc, \zvar and others) are explained in the View+Edit tab chapter. This chapter explains the settings that turn these parts on and off, and the table of variables (the values that PTXprint puts into the front matter, such as the main title).

View levels: In the Basic view this tab shows only Table of Contents, Local Front Matter and the variables table. All other settings on this tab are only shown in the Default and Full views. When one of the main options on this tab is turned on, the name of the tab is shown in a different colour, so you can see that the tab is in use.

Cover

PTXprint can make a cover for the book: a back cover, a spine (the narrow back edge of a bound book) and a front cover, all on one wide page (the "cover spread"). PTXprint saves the cover in its own PDF file. The file has the same name as the main PDF, with _cover at the end. Printers usually print the cover on different paper, so they want it as a separate file.

  • Tick Create Cover Page to make a cover each time you print.
  • Click Cover Wizard... to design the cover step by step (see below).
  • The four links Back Cover, Spine, Front Cover and Cover Spread open the matching style on the Styles tab. Each part of the cover is a sidebar (a box). There you can change its background colour, background picture, border and other box settings. Use Cover Spread for things that go across the whole cover, for example one picture behind the back, spine and front.

The text on each part of the cover comes from special sections of the front matter (coverfront, coverspine and coverback, plus coverwhole for the whole spread). So the cover needs Local Front Matter. If you untick Local Front Matter, PTXprint also unticks Create Cover Page and shows a message about it. If the front matter has no cover sections, no cover is made. The easiest way to create these sections is the Cover Wizard.

There is no separate Cover tab in this version of PTXprint. Use the Cover Wizard and the four style links instead.

The Cover Wizard

Click Cover Wizard... (you must tick Create Cover Page first). A window opens. The steps are on the left and a preview of the whole cover is on the right. Use Next and Back to move between the steps.

  1. Book and Spine Setup – type the approximate number of pages. PTXprint fills this in from the last PDF if it can. Choose whether the book has a spine (most books with fewer than about 80 pages do not have spine text). If it has a spine, choose Paperback or Hardcover, and choose how to find the spine width: Automatic (from the paper weight in gsm or the paper thickness in µm) or Manual (type the width in mm). Ask your printer for the paper thickness if you can. Tick the right-to-left binding option for books in scripts such as Arabic or Hebrew, which open on the other side.
  2. Picture / decoration – choose where the main picture goes (no picture, across the whole cover, front only, front and spine, back only, back and spine, or separate pictures for front and back). Choose the picture file, how it fits (stretch or crop), and its opacity. You can also add a decorative border to the front cover.
  3. Background – white, or a solid colour behind everything. (Gradient shading is not available yet.)
  4. Front cover text – type the title (you must type a title before you can go on). You can also add a subtitle, the language name and a picture. Move the position slider of each item to place it higher or lower on the front cover. You can also change its colour and size.
  5. Spine text (only when the book has a spine) – choose what to show on the spine (title, subtitle, language name), its colour, size, direction and position. (The publisher name on the spine is not available yet.)
  6. Back cover – add a short text (a "blurb"), an ISBN barcode and a logo, and choose where they go.
  7. Review – check the summary and the preview, then click Finish.

When you click Finish, PTXprint:

  • writes new cover sections into the front matter (this replaces any cover sections that were there before);
  • changes the cover styles (background, border, picture, title colours and sizes);
  • puts the title, subtitle, language name and ISBN into the variables maintitle, subtitle, languagename and isbn in the variables table on this tab.

Cancel closes the wizard without changing anything. PTXprint remembers your wizard answers with the configuration, so you can open the wizard again later and make changes.

Front Matter PDF(s) and Back Matter PDF(s)

Use these when part of the book already exists as a PDF file, for example a title page made in another program, or a set of maps or an index made elsewhere.

  • Tick Front Matter PDF(s) and click Select... to choose one or more PDF files that go before the Scripture text.
  • Tick Back Matter PDF(s) and click Select... to choose PDF files that go after the Scripture text.

The names of the chosen files are shown next to the button. Hold the mouse over Select... to see the full path of each file. The PDF pages must have the same page size as your publication.

Table of Contents

Tick Table of Contents to let PTXprint make a table of contents (a list of the books with their page numbers). It is useful when you print several books.

  • Title – the heading of the table of contents, for example "Contents" in your language.
  • Use \toc1 / \toc2 / \toc3 – each book in Paratext has up to three names: \toc1 (the long name), \toc2 (the short name) and \toc3 (the abbreviation). Each name that you tick becomes one column in the table of contents. At least one must be ticked.
  • Leaders – dots or a line between the book name and the page number.

Where does the table of contents appear?

  • If Local Front Matter is not ticked, PTXprint makes its own contents page with your title before the Scripture text.
  • If Local Front Matter is ticked, the table of contents appears where the front matter has the code \ztoc|main\* (see the View+Edit tab chapter). The BASIC front matter template already contains this code.

PTXprint can only know the page numbers after the text has been typeset. It therefore typesets the publication more than once when you click Print. If Quick Run is ticked, it typesets only once. Then the status line says "Rerun to fix: table of contents", and you must click Print again.

Local Front Matter

PTXprint does not print the FRT (front matter) book of your Paratext project directly. It keeps its own copy for each configuration. You change this copy on the View+Edit tab. Tick Local Front Matter to print it. The first time you tick it, PTXprint makes a simple front matter for you (title page, copyright page and table of contents) if there is none yet.

  • Edit... takes you to the Front Matter sub-tab of the View+Edit tab.
  • Force Page Break at each Periph – each section of the front matter (title page, copyright page, preface …) starts on a new page. Leave it ticked unless you want short sections to share a page.
  • Suppress Blank Page Before Scripture Text – normally the Scripture text starts on a right-hand page, and PTXprint adds a blank page when needed. Tick this to stop the blank page.
  • Use Peripheral Introductory Sections – see below.

Note: When you tick Local Front Matter, PTXprint unticks Colophon at End of Publication, because most front matter already has a copyright page. When you untick Local Front Matter, PTXprint ticks the colophon again (and turns off the cover). Check these two settings after you change one of them.

Use Peripheral Introductory Sections

Some projects have an INT (introductions) book in Paratext, with sections such as an introduction to the Old Testament or to the Gospels. Each section starts with a \periph line that has an id. Tick Use Peripheral Introductory Sections to make PTXprint put each section in front of the first book of its group. The ids that PTXprint knows are:

id Placed before
intbible the first book of the Bible
intot the first Old Testament book
intpent the first book of the Pentateuch (GEN–DEU)
inthistory the first history book (JOS–EST)
intpoetry the first poetry book (JOB–SNG)
intprophesy the first book of the prophets (ISA–MAL)
intdc the first Deuterocanon book
intnt the first New Testament book
intgospels the first Gospel (MAT–JHN)
intepistles the first letter of Paul (ROM–PHM)
intletters the first of the other letters (HEB–REV)

The section is only printed when a book of that group is in the list of books to print. Force Page Break at each Periph also decides whether these sections start on a new page.

Maps

  • Add Maps... opens the Add Map dialog. There you choose map pictures, and PTXprint writes one page for each map into a map book (usually XXM). This dialog is explained in the Pictures tab chapter.
  • Include Maps adds the map book to the list of books to print (and changes the Basic tab to Multiple Books if needed). Untick it to take the map book out of the list again. PTXprint saves the configuration when you change this setting.
  • Edit... shows the map book on the View+Edit tab. Nothing happens if there is no map book yet.

Colophon at End of Publication

A colophon is a short text at the very end of the book, for example the copyright, the licence and the picture credits. Tick Colophon at End of Publication to show the text box. PTXprint prints the colophon after the end of the last book.

  • Type the colophon in the Colophon Text box. You can use USFM markers such as \pc (centred paragraph) and the special codes \zcopyright, \zlicense and \zimagecopyrights (see the View+Edit tab chapter).
  • The reset button below the box puts back the standard colophon (copyright, licence, a blank line and the picture credits). For a diglot it also adds the copyright of the second language. Anything you typed is replaced.
  • Force Page Break Before Colophon puts the colophon on a new page at the end, instead of under the last lines of the last book.

The picture credits (\zimagecopyrights) need the page numbers of the pictures. Click Print a second time to get correct picture credits.

Variables and Values

This table lists the variables used in the front matter (and in the colophon and cover). A variable is a place-holder such as \zvar|maintitle\*. When you print, PTXprint puts the value from this table in its place. The values are saved with the configuration. So two configurations can use the same kind of front matter with different titles.

The table has three columns:

  • Pub – tick this to make the variable a field of each publication on the Publications tab. Then each publication can have its own value (for example its own title). maintitle and subtitle are always used there.
  • Name – the name of the variable. You cannot change it here.
  • Value – click the value to change it. Press Enter to keep the new value.

Buttons:

  • Rescan peripheral variables looks for all \zvar|...\* codes in the front matter and adds any missing ones to the table with the value <Type Value Here>. It saves the front matter first.
  • Add asks for the name of a new variable. Use only letters, numbers and hyphens, and no spaces (for example printedby or maintitlefr).
  • Del deletes the selected variables.

The variable toctitle is special: it always uses the Title of the Table of Contents, so it is not in this table.

Common tasks

Add a title page and a copyright page

  1. On the Basic tab, check the copyright and licence statements.
  2. On the Peripherals tab, tick Local Front Matter. PTXprint makes a simple front matter if there is none.
  3. In the Variables and Values table, click the value of maintitle and type the title. Do the same for subtitle and any other variables.
  4. Click Print.

To change the layout of these pages, click Edit... (see the View+Edit tab chapter).

Add a table of contents

  1. On the Basic tab, choose Multiple Books and the books to print.
  2. On the Peripherals tab, tick Table of Contents.
  3. Type the Title, for example "Contents" in your language.
  4. Tick the book names to use (\toc1, \toc2, \toc3) and choose the Leaders.
  5. If Local Front Matter is ticked, make sure that the front matter contains \ztoc|main\* (the BASIC template has it).
  6. Click Print. If the status line asks you to rerun, click Print again.

Make a cover

  1. Tick Local Front Matter (a cover needs it).
  2. Tick Create Cover Page.
  3. Click Cover Wizard..., go through the steps and click Finish.
  4. Click Print. The cover is saved as a separate PDF whose name ends with _cover.
  5. To fine-tune colours, borders or pictures, click Front Cover, Spine, Back Cover or Cover Spread and change the style on the Styles tab.

Add an existing PDF before or after the Scripture text

  1. Tick Front Matter PDF(s) (or Back Matter PDF(s)).
  2. Click Select... and choose one or more PDF files.
  3. Click Print.

Put the copyright and picture credits at the end of the book

  1. Tick Colophon at End of Publication.
  2. If the box is empty, click the reset button under the box to get the standard text.
  3. Tick Force Page Break Before Colophon if you want it on its own page.
  4. Click Print, and then Print again, so that the picture credits are correct.

Add your own variable

  1. Click Add, type a name such as printedby, and click OK.
  2. Click the Value of the new row and type the text.
  3. On the View+Edit tab, put \zvar|printedby\* in the front matter where the text should appear.

Insert book group introductions from the INT book

  1. In Paratext, give each section of the INT book an id, for example \periph New Testament Introduction|id="intnt".
  2. On the Peripherals tab, tick Use Peripheral Introductory Sections.
  3. Print a set of books that includes a book of that group (for example MAT for intnt).

Common problems

The cover is not created. Check that Local Front Matter and Create Cover Page are both ticked. The front matter must contain cover sections. Run the Cover Wizard and click Finish to create them. Remember that the cover is in a separate PDF file (name ending in _cover), not in the main PDF.

Create Cover Page became unticked by itself. You unticked Local Front Matter. A cover cannot be made without it. Tick both again.

The Cover Wizard button is greyed out. Tick Create Cover Page first.

The Finish button in the Cover Wizard is greyed out. You must type a title in the front cover step, and you must be on the last (review) step.

My hand-made changes to the cover text disappeared. Finish in the Cover Wizard replaces the cover sections of the front matter. Make the changes again on the View+Edit tab after you use the wizard.

The colophon disappeared after I turned on Local Front Matter. PTXprint unticks Colophon at End of Publication when you tick Local Front Matter. Tick the colophon again if you want both.

The table of contents is empty or the page numbers are wrong. Click Print again (especially if Quick Run is ticked). If Local Front Matter is ticked, the front matter must contain \ztoc|main\*. Check that at least one of \toc1/\toc2/\toc3 is ticked and that the books have those markers in Paratext.

A book is missing from the table of contents. The book has no text for the ticked \toc markers. Add the \toc1 (or \toc2, \toc3) line to the book in Paratext, or tick another \toc option.

The picture credits in the colophon or front matter are wrong or empty. Click Print a second time. PTXprint needs a first run to find the page of each picture.

A variable prints as "". Click its Value in the Variables and Values table and type the text.

A variable I deleted came back. Rescan peripheral variables (and generating front matter) adds every variable that is used in the front matter. Remove the \zvar code from the front matter first, then delete the row.

There is a blank page before the Scripture text. PTXprint starts the Scripture text on a right-hand page. Tick Suppress Blank Page Before Scripture Text if you do not want this.

The maps are printed although I do not want them. Untick Include Maps. This takes the map book out of the list of books to print.

Most of the settings on this tab are missing. You are using the Basic view. Change to the Default or Full view.

Settings reference: Peripherals tab (front and back matter)

Every control in this part of PTXprint is listed below, grouped by where it appears.

Peripherals tab

Create Cover Page

  • Where: Peripherals tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • Description: Create an outer Cover
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • This tab/section appears when: “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Create a cover (back, spine and front) as a separate PDF file ending in _cover.pdf. Needs Local Front Matter. Use the Cover Wizard... to design it.

Explanation:

Makes a cover each time you print, and saves it as a separate PDF whose name ends with _cover. The cover pages are taken out of the main PDF. It needs Local Front Matter, because the cover text is kept in cover sections of the front matter; if you untick Local Front Matter, this is unticked too. Use Cover Wizard... to create the cover sections.

Cover Wizard...

  • Where: Peripherals tab
  • Type: Button
  • Description: Generate Cover (Basic settings to create a cover)
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Create Cover Page” is selected
  • This tab/section appears when: “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Creating a cover from nothing takes a lot of effort. This tool enables you to create various kinds of covers which can easily be enhanced.

Explanation:

Opens the Cover Wizard, which leads you through 6 or 7 steps (page count and spine, pictures, background, front text, spine text, back cover, review) with a live preview. Finish writes the cover sections into the front matter, sets the cover styles, and fills in the maintitle, subtitle, languagename and isbn variables. Any cover sections that were in the front matter before are replaced. Greyed out until Create Cover Page is ticked.

Back Cover

  • Where: Peripherals tab
  • Type: Link
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • This tab/section appears when: “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Click to edit the Sidebar properties on the Styles tab for the Back Cover.

Explanation:

Opens the Styles tab at the style of the back cover box. Change its background colour, background picture, border or padding there. The text of the back cover is in the coverback section of the front matter.

Spine

  • Where: Peripherals tab
  • Type: Link
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • This tab/section appears when: “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Click to edit the Sidebar properties on the Styles tab for the Spine.

Explanation:

Opens the Styles tab at the style of the spine box (background, border, text direction). The spine text is in the coverspine section of the front matter.

Front Cover

  • Where: Peripherals tab
  • Type: Link
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • This tab/section appears when: “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Click to edit the Sidebar properties on the Styles tab for the Front Cover.

Explanation:

Opens the Styles tab at the style of the front cover box. Use it to change the front background colour or picture, or the border. The front cover text is in the coverfront section of the front matter.

Cover Spread

  • Where: Peripherals tab
  • Type: Link
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • This tab/section appears when: “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Click to edit the Sidebar properties on the Styles tab for the whole Cover Spread (the background behind the back, spine and front).

Explanation:

Opens the Styles tab at the style for the whole cover spread (back, spine and front together). It is the bottom layer: the back, spine and front boxes are placed on top of it. Use it for a background colour or one picture that goes across the whole cover.

Front Matter PDF(s)

  • Where: Peripherals tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • Description: Enable import of front matter PDF(s)
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • This tab/section appears when: “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

One or more previously created PDF file(s) can be included BEFORE the scripture material being typeset. If more than one file is selected, then these will appear in alphabetical order.

If you are creating an electronic publication and want to add a fancy (colour) cover, then consider designing a cover using the online Canva.com tool.

Explanation:

Adds ready-made PDF pages before the Scripture text (and before the local front matter). Use it for pages made in another program. The pages should have the same page size as the publication. Select... is greyed out until this box is ticked.

Select...

  • Where: Peripherals tab
  • Type: Button
  • Description: Select front matter PDF(s) to import
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Front Matter PDF(s)” is selected
  • This tab/section appears when: “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

Explanation:

Choose one or more PDF files. Hold the Ctrl key to choose several. The file names are then shown next to the button, and the full paths are shown when you hold the mouse over the button. To change the list, click the button again and choose all the files you want.

Table of Contents Title

  • Where: Peripherals tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • Description: Enable table of contents
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • This tab/section appears when: “Table of Contents Title”, “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

This will automatically generate the Table of Contents for all the books included in the publication using one or more of the \toc1, \toc2 and \toc3 fields as specified. This option is ignored unless the "Multiple Books" option has been set on the Basic tab.

NOTE: PTXprint typesets the text more than once to get the page numbers right, so printing takes longer. (With Quick Run on, click Print a second time.) If Local Front Matter is on, put \ztoc|main\* in the front matter where the ToC should appear.

Explanation:

Turns on the automatic table of contents. Without Local Front Matter, PTXprint makes its own contents page with the Title. With Local Front Matter, the table appears where the front matter has \ztoc|main\*. PTXprint typesets several times to get the page numbers right, so printing takes longer. With Quick Run ticked, click Print twice.

Table of contents title

  • Where: Peripherals tab
  • Type: Text box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Table of Contents Title” is selected
  • This tab/section appears when: “Table of Contents Title”, “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

The heading for the Table of Contents (for example 'Contents' in your language). It can also be used in the front matter as \zvar|toctitle\*

Explanation:

The heading of the table of contents, in the language of the publication. PTXprint uses it on its own contents page, and the front matter can use it with \zvar|toctitle\*.

Table of contents: Use \toc1

  • Where: Peripherals tab
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Table of Contents Title” is selected
  • This tab/section appears when: “Table of Contents Title”, “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Select which of the \toc markers should be included in the generated Table of Contents.

Explanation:

Uses the long book names (\toc1 in Paratext) as a column of the table of contents. Ticked by default. If you untick all three \toc options, PTXprint ticks this one again.

Table of contents: Use \toc2

  • Where: Peripherals tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Table of Contents Title” is selected
  • This tab/section appears when: “Table of Contents Title”, “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Select which of the \toc markers should be included in the generated Table of Contents.

Explanation:

Uses the short book names (\toc2) as a column of the table of contents. Tick it if you want short names instead of, or as well as, the long names.

Table of contents: Use \toc3

  • Where: Peripherals tab
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Table of Contents Title” is selected
  • This tab/section appears when: “Table of Contents Title”, “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Select which of the \toc markers should be included in the generated Table of Contents.

Explanation:

Uses the book abbreviations (\toc3) as a column of the table of contents. Ticked by default. If you use thumb tabs, the thumb tabs can also show the \toc3 text; when this is unticked, the thumb tab text must come from \zthumbtab instead.

Leaders

  • Where: Peripherals tab
  • Type: Drop-down list
  • Description: Style of leaders for table of contents
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Choices: None; ......................; . . . . . . . . . . . . .; - - - - - - - - -; ________________
  • Only available when: “Table of Contents Title” is selected
  • This tab/section appears when: “Table of Contents Title”, “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Leaders display dots or a line between the text and the page number. Select the style of leader you wish to apply.

Explanation:

The characters between each book name and its page number: close dots, spaced dots, dashes, or a solid line. None leaves the space empty. Leaders help the reader follow the line across a wide page.

Use Peripheral Introductory Sections

  • Where: Peripherals tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • This tab/section appears when: “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Check this option if the INT book contains peripheral divisions (sub-sections) which need to be inserted at the appropriate position between books. For example:
\periph Old Testament Introduction|id="intot"
\periph New Testament Introduction|id="intnt"
\periph Gospels Introduction|id="intgospels"

Explanation:

Inserts sections of the INT book in front of the matching group of books, using the \periph ids such as intot, intnt or intgospels (see the table in this chapter). A section is only printed if a book of its group is being printed. Leave it unticked if your project has no INT book with such sections.

Local Front Matter

  • Where: Peripherals tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • Description: Enable (local) front matter
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • This tab/section appears when: “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

PTXprint does not directly typeset the FRT book from Paratext. Instead, it uses a "local" PTXprint-specific copy of Paratext's FRT book which can be enhanced by additional codes which are described on the View+Edit tab's Information button.

Note: turning this on turns the Colophon off (you can turn it on again). A cover needs Local Front Matter.

Explanation:

Prints the PTXprint front matter for this configuration (edited on the View+Edit tab). The first time, PTXprint creates a simple front matter if there is none. Ticking this unticks Colophon at End of Publication; unticking it ticks the colophon again and turns off Create Cover Page.

Edit...

  • Type: Button
  • Description: View (or edit) front matter
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Local Front Matter” is selected
  • This tab/section appears when: “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication” is ticked

Explanation:

Goes to the Front Matter sub-tab of the View+Edit tab, where you can change the text of the front matter.

Force Page Break at each Periph

  • Where: Peripherals tab
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • Description: Front matter: Force page break at each periph section
  • View level: Default and Full views

Starts each \periph section of the front matter (and each introduction section from the INT book) on a new page. Untick it only if you want short sections, such as a copyright notice and a dedication, to follow each other on one page.

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Enter your Colophon text here - using standard USFM codes for formatting. You may want to use the reset button to start with a standard set.

You can use the following codes to automatically include special text using the following markers:
\zcopyright - copyright statement from the Basic tab
\zlicense - License text from the Basic tab
\zimagecopyrights - Automatically generated list of images, page numbers and attributions.
\zimagecopyrightsfr - as above, but use localized (fr = French) version (es, fr, hu, id, pt, ro available).

\b can be used to insert a blank line between markers if needed.

If using a Left-to-Right script for the colophon in a RTL publication you will need to add \beginL to force the colophon to render LTR. For example:
\pc \beginL \zcopyright
\pc \beginL \zlicense
\pc \beginL \zimagecopyrights

These special codes may also be used in other books such as the front matter book (FRT).

Publications tab

What this tab is for

Sometimes you want to make several similar books from one project with the same design. For example: one PDF for each Gospel, or a New Testament and a separate book of Psalms, each with its own title. The Publications tab lets you do this without making a new configuration for each book.

A publication here means: this configuration, printed with

  • its own list of books, and
  • its own values for some of the variables of the front matter (for example the main title and the subtitle).

All other settings (page size, fonts, layout, front matter, cover and so on) come from the current configuration. You make a list of publications, tick the ones you want, and click Print Selected. PTXprint then makes one PDF for each ticked publication.

This tab is only shown in the Default and Full views.

The list of publications

The list has three columns:

  • Print – tick the publications that you want to print. The checkbox in the column heading ticks or unticks all publications at once.
  • Publication ID / Field – on the first (bold) line of each publication, this is the name of the publication. Under it are the names of its fields (variables).
  • Books / Value – on the bold line, the books to print. Under it, the value of each field for this publication.

Click the small arrow beside a publication (or double-click its line) to show or hide its fields. Expand All and Collapse All do this for all publications.

To change a value, click it, type the new text and press Enter. You can change:

  • the name of a publication (the bold text in the second column). Each name must be different. The name is also used in the name of the PDF file, so keep it short and simple;
  • the books of a publication (the bold text in the third column);
  • the value of each field.

You cannot change the names of the fields here. They come from the variables table on the Peripherals tab (see below).

The books

Type the books in the same way as on the Basic tab, for example:

  • MRK – one book;
  • RUT JON – several books;
  • MAT-JHN – a range of books;
  • JHN 1-5 – some chapters of one book.

You can also type the name of a module file (a file that lists which parts of the text to print). If PTXprint cannot understand the books, the text turns red. Hold the mouse over it to see what is wrong.

The fields

Each publication always has the fields maintitle and subtitle. To add more fields, go to the Peripherals tab and tick Pub beside a variable in the Variables and Values table. The variable is then added to every publication. Untick Pub to remove it again (except for maintitle and subtitle).

When you print a publication, PTXprint uses its values instead of the values on the Peripherals tab. This only changes that one PDF. The values on the Peripherals tab are not changed. For this to work, the front matter (or the cover) must use the variables, for example \zvar|maintitle\* on the title page.

If the book has a cover with a spine, there is also a pagecount field. It holds the number of pages of that publication. PTXprint uses it to work out the width of the spine for that publication's cover.

The buttons

  • Add makes a new publication from the current settings: the books chosen on the Basic tab, and the current values of the variables. Its name is the main title (or "New publication"). It is ticked for printing.
  • Duplicate makes a copy of the highlighted publication, called "Copy of ...". This is the quickest way to make a set of similar publications: duplicate, then change the name, books and title.
  • Delete removes the highlighted publication, after asking you.
  • Expand All / Collapse All show or hide the fields of all publications.
  • Print Selected prints every ticked publication.

The line at the bottom shows how many publications are ticked, and how many have books that PTXprint cannot understand.

Printing the publications

When you click Print Selected, PTXprint:

  1. saves the configuration (including the list of publications);
  2. checks the books of each ticked publication. If some are wrong, it asks if it should print the others and skip these;
  3. prints the publications in the background, several at the same time. The number at the same time is set by Maximum parallel processes on the Advanced tab;
  4. opens the folder with the PDFs when all are finished.

Each PDF is named after the project, the configuration and the publication name. The PDFs are not shown in the PDF preview. Open them from the folder.

While the publications are printing, Print Selected is greyed out.

The list of publications is saved with the configuration.

Common tasks

Make one PDF for each Gospel

  1. On the Peripherals tab, tick Local Front Matter and make sure the title page uses \zvar|maintitle\* (the standard front matter does).
  2. On the Publications tab, click Add.
  3. Click the bold name and type Matthew. Click the books and type MAT.
  4. Open the publication and click the value of maintitle. Type the title of Matthew in your language.
  5. Click Duplicate. Change the copy's name to Mark, its books to MRK, and its title.
  6. Do the same for Luke and John.
  7. Tick all four and click Print Selected.

Give each publication its own value for another variable

  1. On the Peripherals tab, in the Variables and Values table, tick Pub beside the variable (for example isbn).
  2. On the Publications tab, open each publication and type its value.

Print only some of the publications

  1. Untick all publications with the checkbox in the Print column heading.
  2. Tick the ones you want.
  3. Click Print Selected.

Remove a publication

  1. Click the publication (or one of its fields).
  2. Click Delete, then confirm.

Common problems

Print Selected is greyed out. No publication is ticked, or PTXprint is still printing the last set.

Duplicate and Delete are greyed out. Click a publication in the list first.

The books are shown in red. PTXprint cannot understand the list of books. Hold the mouse over the red text to see the problem. Use the 3-letter book codes, separated by spaces, for example GEN EXO.

"None of the selected publications can be printed". All ticked publications have no books or wrong books. Correct the books.

All the PDFs have the same title. The front matter does not use the variable, or it uses a different variable. Check that the title page contains \zvar|maintitle\* (see the View+Edit tab chapter), and that Local Front Matter is ticked on the Peripherals tab.

A variable is not in the publications. Tick Pub beside the variable on the Peripherals tab.

"A publication called ... already exists". Each publication needs a different name. Choose another name.

The Publications tab is missing. You are using the Basic or Minimal view. Change to Default or Full.

Every control in this part of PTXprint is listed below, grouped by where it appears.

Finishing tab

What this tab is for

The Finishing tab controls what happens to the PDF after the pages have been typeset. Come here when you are getting ready to send the book to a printer, or when you want to print it yourself as a folded booklet.

On this tab you can:

  • choose the PDF Output Format that your printer asks for (for example CMYK or black and white);
  • add crop marks and a watermark (such as the word "DRAFT");
  • print the pages as a booklet (two or more pages on each sheet of paper, in the right order for folding);
  • compare the new PDF with an older one, to see exactly what changed;
  • keep older copies of the PDF, and store your settings inside the PDF.

The Finishing tab is shown in the Default and Full views. Some settings are only shown in the Full view. This is noted for each setting below.

Most settings on this tab do not change the layout of the text. They change the finished PDF file. You must click Print (make the PDF again) before a change is visible.

Some print-shop words in simple terms

  • Trim size – the size of the finished book page, after the printer cuts it. In PTXprint this is the Page Size on the Layout tab.
  • Crop marks (also called trim marks) – thin lines in the corners, outside the page, that show the printer where to cut.
  • Bleed – a picture or colour that goes right to the edge of the page. The printer needs it to go a little past the cut line (usually about 3 mm), so that no white strip shows if the cut is not exact.
  • RGB – the colours used by screens (Red, Green, Blue).
  • CMYK – the four inks used by most colour printing presses (Cyan, Magenta, Yellow and blacK). Many printers ask for CMYK files.
  • Grayscale (B/W) – only black ink, in shades of grey.
  • Spot colour – one extra, ready-mixed ink (often a Pantone colour) used in addition to black, for example red for the words of Jesus or for headings.
  • PDF/X – a type of PDF made for printing. It contains everything the printer needs (fonts, colour information) and nothing that could cause problems.
