    • PDF/X-1a – the older, strict type. All colours must be CMYK (or grey/spot) and there may be no transparency (see-through effects). Many printing presses still ask for this.
    • PDF/X-4 – the newer type. It allows RGB colours with colour profiles and transparency. Many modern printers and digital (print-on-demand) printers accept it.
  • PDF/A – a type of PDF made for keeping documents for a very long time (archiving).
  • Imposition – arranging several book pages on one large sheet of paper, so that after folding and cutting the pages come out in the right order.
  • Signature – a group of sheets that are folded together and sewn or glued into the book as one unit.

If your printer gives you a list of requirements, read it carefully. Look for: trim size, bleed, crop marks (yes or no), colour (CMYK, grey, or RGB), and PDF type (PDF/X-1a or PDF/X-4). Then set these on the Layout tab and on this tab. If you are not sure, ask the printer for a sample "print-ready PDF specification".

PDF Details

This area controls the type of PDF that PTXprint makes. (This area is shown in the Default and Full views. Some settings are only in the Full view.)

PDF Output Format

Choose the format that matches how the book will be used:

  • Screen (Quickest) – the normal choice while you are still working on the book. PTXprint makes the PDF directly, with no extra processing. Use this for checking and proof-reading.
  • Digital-RGB – a PDF/X-4 file in RGB colours. Good for reading on screen, for sharing as an e-book, and for printing on an office or home printer.
  • Digital-CMYK (Transparency) – a PDF/X-4 file for printers who want CMYK but can accept transparency.
  • Print-CMYK – a PDF/X-1a file with all colours turned into CMYK. Use this for a commercial printing press that asks for PDF/X-1a or CMYK.
  • Print-Gray (B/W) – a PDF/X-1a file in black and shades of grey only. Use this for a book printed only in black ink. Coloured text and pictures are turned into grey.
  • Print-Spot – black plus one spot colour. Any colour close to the Color Hue you choose is printed with the spot ink; everything else is printed in black and grey. The Color Hue and Tolerance (%) settings are only active when you choose this format.

The formats other than Screen need extra processing after the PDF is made. This takes more time, especially when the book has many pictures. PTXprint shows a note in the status bar about this.

PTXprint adds a short ending to the PDF file name, so you can see which format a file has: _RGB, _CMYK-Transparent, _CMYK, _BW or _Spot. Screen adds nothing.

When you choose Print-CMYK, Print-Gray or Print-Spot and thumb tabs are turned on, PTXprint turns on Only Show on Odd Pages for the thumb tabs (on the Tabs+Borders tab), and tells you in the status bar.

Other PDF settings

  • Crop Marks adds cut lines around every page. To make room for them, PTXprint makes each PDF page larger by 0.5 inch (about 12.7 mm) on every side. Only turn this on if your printer asks for crop marks. Many print-on-demand printers do not want them.
  • Number of Previous PDFs to be Kept keeps older copies of your PDF (with _1, _2 … at the end of the name). You need at least 1 to use Compare PDFs with the previous version.
  • Include Config Settings Within PDF stores your settings inside the PDF file. Later, you (or someone else) can load the settings back from this PDF, using Import Settings.
  • Archive (PDF/A-4) makes a PDF that is better for long-term storage. (Only in the Full view.)
  • Extract Color Inserts and Extra XDV Processing are special tools. (Only in the Full view.)
  • Apply Watermark PDF puts a PDF (for example "DRAFT") on every page.

Booklet Pagination

This area lets you print several book pages on one larger sheet of paper, arranged so that you can fold the sheets into a booklet. This is called imposition. (This area is shown in the Basic, Default and Full views. Some settings are only in the Full view.)

  • Pages Per Spread – how many book pages go on one side of a sheet. 1-up (No booklet) is the normal setting: one page per PDF page. 2-up is a normal folded booklet: for example, A5 pages on A4 paper. 4-up and 8-up put more pages on bigger sheets, for printers who fold the sheet more than once.
  • Physical Paper Size – the size of the sheet you will print on. For 2-up, it is normally twice the page size (A5 pages → A4 sheet).
  • Sheets Per Signature, Fold Cut Margin (mm) and Fold First are for professional binding. (Only in the Full view.) Leave them at their starting values unless the printer tells you what to use.

When Pages Per Spread is more than 1-up:

  • the signature settings become active;
  • Scale to fit is greyed out;
  • the Finishing tab label changes colour, to remind you that the PDF will be imposed;
  • the PDF file name gets an extra ending, such as _2up;
  • crop marks (if ticked) are drawn on the large sheet, not on each page.

When Pages Per Spread is 1-up, you can tick Scale to fit. Then PTXprint enlarges or shrinks each page so that it fits the Physical Paper Size, centred on the sheet.

If the pages do not fit on the paper you chose, PTXprint shows a Paper Size Error. Choose a larger Physical Paper Size or a smaller number of pages per spread.

Compare PDFs

This area makes a "diff" PDF that shows what changed between the new PDF and an older one. This is very useful after a late correction: you can quickly check that only the expected pages changed. (The two colour settings are only shown in the Full view. Show Max Diff Pages is shown in the Default and Full views.)

How it works:

  1. PTXprint keeps a copy of the previous PDF (the file ending _1.pdf), as long as Number of Previous PDFs to be Kept is 1 or more.
  2. When Compare PDFs is ticked and you click Print, PTXprint makes the new PDF and then compares it with the old one.
  3. If it finds differences, it makes a file ending _diff.pdf and opens it. Added or moved text is shown in one colour; removed text or old positions in another colour.
  4. If there are no differences, the status bar says No differences found.

By default PTXprint compares with the previous PDF (Previous PDF (_1)). Click Select... to compare with any other PDF instead, for example the PDF you sent for the last proof check.

Common tasks

Make a PDF for a commercial printer who asks for PDF/X-1a in CMYK

  1. On the Layout tab, check that the Page Size is the trim size the printer wants.
  2. On the Finishing tab, in the PDF Details area, set PDF Output Format to Print-CMYK.
  3. Tick Crop Marks only if the printer asks for crop marks.
  4. Make sure Pages Per Spread is 1-up (No booklet). Printers do their own imposition.
  5. Click Print. The new PDF name ends with _CMYK.

Make a black-and-white PDF for printing

  1. On the Finishing tab, set PDF Output Format to Print-Gray (B/W).
  2. Click Print. All colours in text and pictures become shades of grey. The file name ends with _BW.

Print an A5 booklet on A4 paper on an office printer

  1. On the Layout tab, set the page size to A5.
  2. On the Finishing tab, in Booklet Pagination, set Pages Per Spread to 2-up.
  3. Set Physical Paper Size to 210mm, 297mm (A4).
  4. Click Print. The new PDF (ending _2up) has two pages side by side on each A4 sheet, in booklet order.
  5. Print it double-sided. For 2-up, choose "flip on short edge" in your printer settings. Print one or two test sheets first.
  6. Fold the stack of sheets in the middle and staple along the fold.

Use a paper size that is not in the list

  1. Click in the Physical Paper Size box and type the width and height, separated by a comma. For example: 203mm, 330mm.
  2. You can use mm or in.

See what changed since the last PDF

  1. On the Finishing tab, check that Number of Previous PDFs to be Kept is at least 1.
  2. Tick Compare PDFs (or press Ctrl+R).
  3. Make your corrections, then click Print.
  4. The "diff" PDF opens and shows the changes in colour. Untick Compare PDFs when you are finished.

Compare with an older proof, not just the last run

  1. In the Compare PDFs area, click Select... and choose the older PDF.
  2. Tick Compare PDFs and click Print.
  3. To go back to comparing with the previous run, click Select... again and click Cancel in the file dialog.

Put "DRAFT" on every page

  1. In the PDF Details area, tick Apply Watermark PDF.
  2. Click Select... next to it. PTXprint opens its own folder of watermarks. Choose the one that matches your page size (for example A5-Draft.pdf).
  3. Click Print.

Send your settings to someone else inside the PDF

  1. Tick Include Config Settings Within PDF (it is ticked by default).
  2. Click Print and send the PDF.
  3. The other person can load your settings from that PDF using Import Settings (see the chapter on importing settings).

Common problems

The colours look different in the printed book from on screen. Screens use RGB. Printing presses use CMYK, which cannot show some bright colours. Choose Print-CMYK (or the format your printer asks for), click Print, and check the result before you send it. Ask the printer for a printed proof if colour is important.

Making the PDF is now very slow. A PDF Output Format other than Screen needs extra processing, especially for pictures. While you are still editing, use Screen (Quickest). Change to the final format only for the last PDF. Also, Compare PDFs adds time, because it renders the pages as images.

The PDF pages are bigger than my page size. Crop Marks is ticked. Crop marks add 0.5 inch (about 12.7 mm) on each side of every page. Untick Crop Marks if the printer did not ask for them.

The PDF is two pages per sheet, or the file name ends with _2up. Pages Per Spread is not set to 1-up (No booklet). Set it back to 1-up for a normal PDF. Commercial printers almost always want single pages (1-up).

I see a "Paper Size Error" message. The book pages do not fit on the Physical Paper Size with the chosen Pages Per Spread. Choose a larger sheet or fewer pages per spread.

"Scale to fit" is greyed out. It only works with 1-up (No booklet). Set Pages Per Spread to 1-up.

"Sheets Per Signature", "Fold Cut Margin" and "Fold First" are greyed out or missing. They are only active when Pages Per Spread is 2-up or more, and they are only shown in the Full view.

"Color Hue" and "Tolerance" are greyed out. They are only used for Print-Spot. Set PDF Output Format to Print-Spot first.

Compare PDFs does not show anything, or says there is nothing to compare. There must be an older PDF to compare with. Check that Number of Previous PDFs to be Kept is at least 1, and click Print once without comparing, so that a previous copy exists. If you used Select..., check that the chosen file still exists.

The watermark is missing or in the wrong place. The watermark PDF should have the same page size as your book. Choose a file that matches your page size. If the watermark file was moved or deleted, PTXprint warns you that it cannot find it. Click Select... again.

The maps (or other insert pages) are missing from my PDF. Extract Color Inserts is ticked. These pages were saved as separate PDF files next to the main PDF. Untick it if you want them inside the main PDF.

Thumb tabs now appear only on odd pages. When you chose Print-CMYK, Print-Gray or Print-Spot, PTXprint turned on Only Show on Odd Pages for thumb tabs. You can change it back on the Tabs+Borders tab.

Settings reference: Finishing tab

Every control in this part of PTXprint is listed below, grouped by where it appears.

Finishing tab › Booklet Pagination

Physical Paper Size

  • Where: Finishing tab › Booklet Pagination
  • Type: Drop-down list
  • Description: Pagination: Physical paper size
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Choices: 420mm, 594mm (A2); 297mm, 420mm (A3); 210mm, 297mm (A4); 17in, 22in (ANSI C); 11in, 17in (ANSI B); 8.5in, 11in (Letter); 353mm, 500mm (B3); 250mm, 353mm (B4); 176mm, 250mm (B5)

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

If the required size is not displayed, then just type the required page width and height separated by a comma.

For example: 203mm, 330mm (Foolscap)

This is the actual size of the sheet of paper on which multiple pages will be printed. For example, if printing an A5-sized booklet, the actual sheet of paper that you print on will be 2x the A5-sized page, which is an A4-sized sheet of paper.

Explanation:

The size of the paper that goes into the printer, not the size of the book page. It is only used when Pages Per Spread is 2-up or more, or when Scale to fit is ticked. For a 2-up booklet, choose a sheet that is twice the book page (A5 book → A4 sheet; Letter-half book → Letter sheet). You can type any size as "width, height", for example 203mm, 330mm. If the pages do not fit, you get a Paper Size Error when you print.

Pages Per Spread

  • Where: Finishing tab › Booklet Pagination
  • Type: Drop-down list
  • Description: Pagination: Pages per spread (booklet printing)
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Choices: 1-up (No booklet); 2-up; 4-up; 8-up

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

How many pages will be printed on one side of the physical paper?

For example, for an A5-sized booklet, 2 pages will fit on each side, making a total of 4 pages on a single sheet.

Explanation:

1-up (No booklet) makes a normal PDF with one book page on each PDF page. This is what commercial and print-on-demand printers want. 2-up makes a simple folded booklet that you can print yourself on double-sided paper. 4-up and 8-up are for sheets that are folded twice or three times, usually by a print shop. When this is more than 1-up, the PDF file name gets an ending like _2up, and the signature settings become active.

Scale to fit

  • Where: Finishing tab › Booklet Pagination
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • Description: Pagination: Scale to fit
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Only available when Pages per Spread is 1-up. Enable this option to scale every page (up or down) so that it fits the Physical Paper Size (set on this tab), centred on the sheet.

Explanation:

Only active when Pages Per Spread is 1-up. PTXprint enlarges or shrinks every page so that it fits the Physical Paper Size, and centres it on the sheet. Use it, for example, to print an A5 proof on A4 paper with larger text. The book layout does not change; only the final PDF is scaled.

Sheets Per Signature

  • Where: Finishing tab › Booklet Pagination
  • Type: Number box
  • Description: Pagination: Sheets per signature (pages per form)
  • View level: Full view only

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

A signature is a collection of pages folded and bound together as a unit. A signature may be made up of multiple sheets.

If unsure, leave this setting at 0 to indicate that the publication will not be bound using separate signatures.

Explanation:

How many sheets of paper are folded together into one signature (one group of pages in the book). 0 means the whole book is one group, like a stapled booklet. Only change this if your printer or binder tells you how many sheets they put in each signature. Only active when Pages Per Spread is 2-up or more.

Fold Cut Margin (mm)

  • Where: Finishing tab › Booklet Pagination
  • Type: Number box
  • Description: Pagination: Minimum fold cut margin
  • View level: Full view only

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

The minimum width of the area to be cut after folding of the signature. Measured in millimeters (mm).

Explanation:

Extra space (in mm) left at the folds of a signature, where the paper will be cut after folding. Only needed for 4-up and 8-up sheets that are folded and then trimmed. Use the value your printer gives you. Leave it at 0 for a simple 2-up booklet.

Fold First

  • Where: Finishing tab › Booklet Pagination
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • Description: Pagination: Fold First
  • View level: Full view only

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

If you are imposing for a printer with a folding machine, then you want to fold first and then cut. This, for example makes a folded sheet that is part of a signature consist of two sets of sequential pages.

Explanation:

Changes the page order on the sheet to suit a print shop that folds the sheets first and cuts them after. Leave it unticked unless the printer asks for "fold first". Only active when Pages Per Spread is 2-up or more.

Create Cover as a Separate PDF

  • Where: Finishing tab › Booklet Pagination
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • Description: Pagination: Create the cover as a stand-alone PDF
  • View level: Full view only

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

This option is only available if Create Cover is enabled on the Cover tab. Enable this option if you plan to print the outer (wrapper) cover separately from the book's content. This is often the case if cardstock, or a colour cover is used.

Explanation:

Most printers print the cover on different paper (thicker card, or colour) from the inside pages, so they want the cover as its own PDF file. When PTXprint makes a cover, it saves the cover pages in a separate PDF whose name ends with _cover.pdf.

Finishing tab

Booklet Pagination

  • Where: Finishing tab
  • Type: Label
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Whether you need a simple booklet or a more complex signature, these options allow plenty of scope.

Compare PDFs

  • Where: Finishing tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • Description: Create 'diff' to Compare PDFs
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Enable this option to generate a PDF showing the differences between the current PDF and the selected previous version (see 'Compare With a Previous PDF' below).

If any differences are found, it should open the "Diff" PDF in the default PDF viewer.

Shortcut: Ctrl-R

Explanation:

When ticked, every Print also makes a "diff" PDF that shows the differences between the new PDF and the comparison PDF (see Select... in the Compare PDFs area). The diff PDF opens automatically. Untick it when you no longer need it, because comparing adds time to each print. When you untick it, PTXprint deletes the old diff file.

Finishing tab › Compare PDFs

Select...

  • Where: Finishing tab › Compare PDFs
  • Type: Button
  • Description: Compare PDFs: Select previous PDF to compare with
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Select a particular PDF file to be compared against the current output PDF. If you just want to compare output to the previous run, then click Cancel in the File Open dialog to reset the filename (which will then default to _1).

Explanation:

By default the comparison is with the previous run (Previous PDF (_1)). Use this button to choose a different PDF, such as the proof you sent for checking last month. The label becomes bold to remind you that a special file is selected. Click Cancel in the file dialog to go back to the previous run.

Only Show Pages With Differences

  • Where: Finishing tab › Compare PDFs
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • Description: Compare PDFs: Only show pages with differences
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

When comparing two PDF files the resulting "Diff" PDF can get rather large. This option reduces the size of the PDF by not including any identical pages. This also saves time as you don't need to search through a lengthy PDF to find out what might have changed.

Explanation:

Leave this ticked. Then the diff PDF contains only the pages that changed, so it is small and quick to check. Untick it only if you want to see every page, changed or not.

Show New Text or Position in

  • Where: Finishing tab › Compare PDFs
  • Type: Colour picker
  • Description: Compare PDFs:
  • View level: Full view only

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Use this color to show anything that has been added (or moved to the current location) in the new PDF.

Set the color to use when differences are found between the old and the new PDFs.

Use this color to show anything that has been added (or moved to the current location) in the new PDF.

Explanation:

The colour used in the diff PDF for new things: text that was added, or text that moved to this place. Choose a colour that is easy to tell apart from the Show Old Text or Position in colour.

Show Old Text or Position in

  • Where: Finishing tab › Compare PDFs
  • Type: Colour picker
  • View level: Full view only

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Use this color to show anything that has been deleted (or moved from the previous location) in the old PDF.

Set the color to use when differences are found between the old and the new PDFs.

Use this color to show anything that has been deleted (or moved from the previous location) in the old PDF.

Explanation:

The colour used in the diff PDF for old things: text that was removed, or the place where moved text used to be. Choose a colour that is easy to tell apart from the Show New Text or Position in colour.

Show Max Diff Pages

  • Where: Finishing tab › Compare PDFs
  • Type: Number box
  • Description: Compare PDFs: Set maximum diff pages to show
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from 1 to 999, default 20

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

The PDF showing differences between the old and the new contains images that make the resulting file rather large. Use this option to limit the number of "Diff" pages created. This will also potentially speed up the process.

Explanation:

The highest number of changed pages that are put into the diff PDF. Each diff page is an image, so many pages make a large file and take time. The default of 20 is usually enough. Increase it if you expect many pages to change, for example after a change that moves text across the whole book.

Finishing tab › PDF Details

PDF Output Format

  • Where: Finishing tab › PDF Details
  • Type: Drop-down list
  • Description: PDF output format (Screen, RGB, CMYK, B/W, spot)
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Choices: Screen (Quickest); Digital-RGB; Digital-CMYK (Transparency); Print-CMYK; Print-Gray (B/W); Print-Spot

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Select the appropriate standard for the output format to optimize the PDF for its intended purpose.

Screen (fastest, no post processing) Digital-RGB (for screens and local printing, PDF/X-4) Digital-CMYK (CMYK, PDF/X-4) Print-CMYK, Print-Gray (B/W), Print-Spot (for professional printers, PDF/X-1a:2003)

Note: Tick 'Archive' to also comply with the archive standard PDF/A-4.

Explanation:

Use Screen (Quickest) while you work. Choose the final format only when you make the PDF for the printer: Print-CMYK for a printer that asks for PDF/X-1a or CMYK; Print-Gray (B/W) for black-ink-only books; Print-Spot for black plus one extra ink; Digital-RGB for screens, e-books and office printers (PDF/X-4). The non-Screen formats take longer to make, especially with many pictures. Each format adds its own ending to the file name (for example _CMYK), so the files do not overwrite each other.

PDF Output Format

  • Where: Finishing tab › PDF Details
  • Type: Label
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Select the appropriate standard for the output format to optimize the PDF for its intended purpose.

Screen (fastest, no post processing) Digital-RGB (for screens and local printing, PDF/X-4) Digital-CMYK (CMYK, PDF/X-4) Print-CMYK, Print-Gray (B/W), Print-Spot (for professional printers, PDF/X-1a:2003)

Note: Tick 'Archive' to also comply with the archive standard PDF/A-4.

Crop Marks

  • Where: Finishing tab › PDF Details
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • Description: Enable crop marks
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Some printers require crop marks on the PDF to show where the page should be trimmed after binding.

Explanation:

Adds cut marks at the corners of each page. PTXprint makes each PDF page 0.5 inch (about 12.7 mm) larger on every side to make room for them. Only tick this if your printer asks for crop marks; many print-on-demand printers reject files with crop marks because the page size is then wrong. When Pages Per Spread is 2-up or more, the marks are drawn on the large sheet instead.

Number of Previous PDFs to be Kept

  • Where: Finishing tab › PDF Details
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: default 1

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

By default, PTXprint only keeps one previous PDF (named ..._1.pdf). Up to 20 previous versions can be kept. Compare PDFs uses the _1 PDF unless you select another one, so keep at least 1.

By keeping previous versions of the PDF, it is possible to compare the final output of the PDFs. Up to 20 previous versions can be kept.

If you need to keep a PDF around longer, then manually rename it so that it can be compared to at a later date.

Explanation:

Before each new PDF is made, PTXprint copies the old one to a file ending _1.pdf (and the older ones to _2.pdf, _3.pdf …). Compare PDFs uses the _1 file, so keep this at 1 or more if you want to compare. Older versions are deleted when the number is reached, so rename a PDF yourself if you must keep it.

Include Config Settings Within PDF

  • Where: Finishing tab › PDF Details
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

All the configuration settings (including the PTXprint styles, AdjLists, changes.txt, and related .tex files) can be included within the PDF in order to maintain a record of what settings were used to create that PDF. Later, these settings can be retrieved from the PDF to set up an identical configuration. This is also a way to share config settings with other users.

Explanation:

Stores your configuration (settings, styles, AdjLists, changes and related files) inside the PDF file. The PDF looks the same. It is a good record of how the PDF was made. You or another person can load these settings back with Import Settings, choosing the PDF as the source. Leave it ticked unless you have a reason not to share your settings with the PDF.

Archive (PDF/A-4)

  • Where: Finishing tab › PDF Details
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • Description: Include unicode text within PDF (to help with archiving)
  • View level: Full view only

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Check this option to include the Unicode text in the PDF which is a good practice for final print and long-term archiving. PDF/A-4 is the currently preferred archival format.

Explanation:

Makes a PDF that follows the PDF/A-4 archive standard. The text in the PDF can then be searched and copied correctly as Unicode, which is good for long-term storage and for digital libraries. Only tick it if you need an archive PDF; it is not needed for normal printing.

Color Hue

  • Where: Finishing tab › PDF Details
  • Type: Colour picker
  • Description: Spot color hue
  • View level: Full view only

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

If a spot color is needed then select the closest hue. Colors close to this hue are printed with the spot ink; everything else in black/gray. Tell your printer which ink to use.

Explanation:

Only active when PDF Output Format is Print-Spot. Choose the colour (hue) of the spot ink, for example the red used for headings. Text and graphics with a similar colour are printed with the spot ink; everything else becomes black and grey. Tell your printer which ink (for example, which Pantone number) they should use for this colour.

Tolerance (%)

  • Where: Finishing tab › PDF Details
  • Type: Number box
  • Description: Spot color tolerance
  • View level: Full view only
  • Values: default 15

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

To match the Spot Color Hue exactly, set this to 0%. If text in similar colors are also to be set to this Spot Color, then select an acceptable tolerance range (suggested default is 15%).

Note that this will include similar colors either side (e.g. -15% to +15%) of the selected hue.

Explanation:

Only active when PDF Output Format is Print-Spot. Sets how close a colour must be to the Color Hue to be printed with the spot ink. 0% means only exactly that hue. The default of 15% also catches slightly different shades. Increase it if some coloured items come out grey; decrease it if items that should be grey come out in the spot colour.

Extract Color Inserts

  • Where: Finishing tab › PDF Details
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • Description: Extract Color Insert pages (as separate PDFs)
  • View level: Full view only

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Extract the special peripheral materials named 'maps' or 'insert_*' as separate PDFs to be printed in color and inserted manually during the binding process.

Note that the cover is always extracted.

Explanation:

Takes special pages out of the main PDF and saves them as separate PDF files: maps, and peripheral pages whose name starts with "insert_". The new file names end with the name of the insert, for example _maps.pdf. Use this when colour pages are printed separately and added to the book during binding. The extracted pages are removed from the main PDF.

Extra XDV Processing

  • Where: Finishing tab › PDF Details
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • Description: Extra XDV processing (before creating final PDF)
  • View level: Full view only

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Enable processing of the intermediate xdv file for such things as coloured diacritics.

Explanation:

Runs an extra processing step before the final PDF is made. It is needed only for a few special features, such as coloured diacritics. Leave it unticked unless a feature you use asks for it, because it makes printing slower.

Apply Watermark PDF

  • Where: Finishing tab › PDF Details
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • Description: Finishing: Apply watermark
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

A watermark can be applied to all pages of the publication. The file must be a PDF and should ideally have the same dimensions as the publication being printed.

Explanation:

Adds a watermark PDF behind every page, for example the word "DRAFT" or a copyright notice. This is helpful for proof copies, so that nobody mistakes them for the finished book. Untick it before you make the final PDF for the printer. The watermark PDF should have the same page size as your book.

Select...

  • Where: Finishing tab › PDF Details
  • Type: Button
  • Description: Finishing: Select watermark to apply
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Apply Watermark PDF” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Choose the watermark PDF file. It should ideally be the same size as the book page.

Explanation:

Only active when Apply Watermark PDF is ticked. Opens PTXprint's own folder of ready-made watermarks (for example A4-Draft.pdf, A5-Draft.pdf, A5-CopyrightWatermark.pdf). Choose one that matches your page size, or choose your own one-page PDF from anywhere on your computer.

Printers tab

What this tab is for

The Printers tab helps you plan the printing of your book. It gives a rough price estimate from several print companies, shows how thick the book will be, and lets you compare prices between printers in a graph. For one printer (Pretore), you can also get an exact quotation and start an order directly from PTXprint.

Come here when the book is nearly finished and you want to know: "About how much will it cost to print 500 copies?", "Which printer is cheapest for this size and number of pages?", or "How thick will the spine be?"

The Printers tab is only shown in the Full view.

Important: most prices on this tab are estimates. PTXprint calculates them from price information collected earlier from each printer. Real prices change, and shipping and taxes are not included. Always get a real quotation from the printer before you make a decision.

The tab has three parts:

  1. Book & Job Specification at the top – the facts about your book and print job.
  2. The printer list – one row for each printer, with an estimated price per copy.
  3. The printer details panel – the options and price details for the printer you click in the list.

Book & Job Specification

These settings describe the job. All printers use them.

  • Pages – the number of pages. PTXprint fills this in from the most recent PDF you made. You can change it, for example to add pages for front matter that is printed separately.
  • Copies – how many books you want to print.
  • Interior – Black & white or Full color for the inside pages.
  • Binding – Paperback (soft cover), Hardcover or Saddle-stitched (stapled). Each printer uses its nearest matching binding. If a printer does not offer your choice, it says so in red in its details panel.
  • Currency – the currency for all prices. PTXprint gets exchange rates from the internet, so prices from printers in other countries can be shown in your currency.
  • Trim size – the finished page size (in mm). This comes from the page size on the Layout tab. You cannot change it here.
  • Thickness – the estimated thickness of the book (spine), for the printer selected in the list. It depends on the number of pages, the paper that printer uses, and the binding. This is useful when you design a cover, because the spine width must match the book thickness.

Every time you change one of these settings, all the prices are calculated again.

The printer list

Each row shows:

  • a Compare tick box;
  • the Printer name, its country and web address;
  • Est. per copy – the estimated price for one copy, at the number of Copies you entered.

Under the price, a small word tells you where the price comes from:

  • estimate – PTXprint calculated it from its own price model for that printer.
  • live quote – the price came from the printer's own system over the internet (Pretore).
  • quote in panel – this printer gives live quotes only. Open its panel and ask for a quotation.
  • no model yet – PTXprint does not have price information for this printer yet. Use its web link to ask for a price.

When two or more printers have a price, the cheapest one is shown in green.

Click a printer's row to see its details panel below or beside the list.

Per Copy and Total Job show the price for the selected printer: for one copy, and for the whole job. The total can be for slightly more copies than you asked for, if that printer rounds the number of copies (see below).

Compare Prices...

Click Compare Prices... to open the Multi-Quote Comparison window. It shows a graph of the price for each printer that is ticked in the Compare column, at several quantities (50, 100, 250, 500 and 1000 copies, plus your own number of Copies).

In this window you can:

  • choose Price per Copy or Total Price;
  • set a Max Budget, so that totals above your budget are left out (tick No limit to show everything);
  • tick or untick printers under Show Printers;
  • tick Show smooth curves to draw curves instead of straight lines between points;
  • point at a dot on the graph to see the exact value.

Printers that have no price model cannot be ticked for comparison. For Pretore, PTXprint asks Pretore's server for prices when you click Compare Prices...; this only works if you have set up a Pretore account (see below).

The printer details panels

Each printer has its own panel with extra options. These options only affect that printer's estimate.

Pothi (India)

  • Paper type – plain white, plain natural shade, or coated paper. For black-and-white books the price does not change with the paper. Coated paper costs more only with a full-colour interior.
  • The panel shows how the price is made up: the Nearest size in Pothi's list of book sizes, the base price, the binding adjustment, the colour cost, and the 1-copy price.
  • A row of prices shows the discount for larger orders (1, 50+, 100+, 250+, 500+, 1000+ copies). The price for your number of copies is in bold.
  • Red warnings appear if the job does not fit Pothi's rules. For example: saddle-stitching only up to 64 pages; soft cover only from 50 to 500 pages; for 1500 or more copies, contact Pothi directly.

Print Gallery (India)

  • Paper type – several paper weights (gsm = grams per square metre; a higher number is thicker paper).
  • Lamination – a thin plastic layer on the cover to protect it.
  • The panel shows the cost of covers, interior, lamination and binding, and how the pages are arranged on Print Gallery's large sheets (Imposition).
  • Print Gallery prints on sheets that hold 4 pages, so the page count is rounded up to a multiple of 4. A5 books are printed in pairs, so an odd number of copies is rounded up by one. A red note tells you when this happens.
  • Stapled binding is not used for books over 100 pages; perfect (glued) binding is priced instead.

Pretore (Netherlands)

Pretore gives live quotations from its own system, and you can start an order from PTXprint. You need a Pretore account and an internet connection.

  • Paper Type, Cover Lamination, Shrink Wrap and Ribbons (marker ribbons, for hardback only) – Pretore's own options.
  • Book Identifier and Description – PTXprint fills these in from the project and the books you are printing. Both must be filled in before you can get a quotation or create an order.
  • Account... – choose your Pretore account, or import an account key file that you downloaded from the Pretore website. The window has a link to register and download the key.
  • Get Precise Quotation – asks Pretore for the real price of this job.
  • Create Order – packs the finished PDF files into a ZIP file and creates an order at Pretore. The order reference, the ZIP file name and the status (awaiting payment) are shown. Use the copy button to copy the full path of the ZIP file.
  • Complete Order & Payment via website – opens the Pretore website, where you upload the ZIP file and pay.

Pretore accepts books of 120 to 2000 pages. It does not offer saddle-stitching (it quotes paperback instead), and its price does not change between black-and-white and colour interiors.

Snowfall Press (United States)

PTXprint does not yet have price information for this printer, so it is left out of comparisons. Use the link in the panel to visit the website and ask for a quotation.

Common tasks

Get a quick price estimate for my book

  1. Make the PDF of the whole book first (click Print), so that the page count is correct.
  2. Change to the Full view if the Printers tab is not visible.
  3. Open the Printers tab. Check Pages and Trim size.
  4. Enter the number of Copies, and choose Interior and Binding.
  5. Choose your Currency.
  6. Read the Est. per copy column. The cheapest printer is shown in green.

Compare prices from several printers in a graph

  1. Fill in the Book & Job Specification as above.
  2. In the printer list, tick Compare for each printer you want in the graph.
  3. Click Compare Prices....
  4. Choose Price per Copy or Total Price. Point at the dots to read exact prices.

Find out how thick the book will be (for the cover spine)

  1. Fill in Pages and Binding.
  2. Click a printer in the list, then choose its paper in its details panel.
  3. Read Thickness. Different printers and papers give different thicknesses. Ask the printer for the exact spine width before you finish the cover.

Order from Pretore

  1. Make the final PDF with the format Pretore asks for (see the Finishing tab).
  2. On the Printers tab, click Pretore in the list.
  3. Click Account... and choose or import your account key.
  4. Choose the paper and other options. Check Book Identifier and Description.
  5. Click Get Precise Quotation and check the price.
  6. Click Create Order. PTXprint makes the ZIP file and shows the order reference.
  7. Click Complete Order & Payment via website to upload the ZIP file and pay.

Common problems

I cannot see the Printers tab. The tab is only shown in the Full view. Change the view level.

The number of pages is 99, or is wrong. PTXprint reads the page count from the last PDF you made for the current books. If you have not made a PDF yet, it shows 99. Click Print first, then come back to the tab. You can also type the correct number into Pages.

A printer shows "—" and no price. Either this printer has no price model yet (no model yet), or it gives live quotes only (quote in panel). For Pretore, set up an account and click Get Precise Quotation. Also check the red warnings in the printer's panel: the job may be outside that printer's limits.

Pretore says "No account configured". Click Account... in the Pretore panel and import the account key file from the Pretore website.

"Get Precise Quotation" and "Create Order" are greyed out. Book Identifier and Description must both be filled in.

"Create Order" says I must print the job first. PTXprint needs the finished PDF files to put in the ZIP file. Click Print, then try again.

The total is for more copies than I asked for. Some printers print in pairs or round the number of copies. A red note in the printer's panel explains this.

I cannot tick a printer in the Compare column. That printer has no price model, so it cannot be compared.

Prices are shown in the wrong currency, or not converted. PTXprint downloads exchange rates from the internet. Without an internet connection (or when Disable ALL Internet Use is ticked on the Advanced tab), prices from another country may be shown in that printer's own currency, or left out of the comparison graph.

Settings reference: Printers tab

Every control in this part of PTXprint is listed below, grouped by where it appears.

Printers tab › Book & Job Specification

Thickness

  • Where: Printers tab › Book & Job Specification
  • Type: Label
  • View level: Full view only

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Spine/book thickness for the currently selected printer, based on its paper stock and binding.

Trim size

  • Where: Printers tab › Book & Job Specification
  • Type: Label
  • View level: Full view only

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Finished page size of the book, from the Layout page settings.

Pages

  • Where: Printers tab › Book & Job Specification
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Full view only
  • Values: from 1 to 9999, default 200

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Number of pages in the book. Filled in automatically from the most recently created PDF (99 if no PDF has been made yet), but can be adjusted manually.

Explanation:

Filled in from the most recent PDF of the selected books. If no PDF has been made yet, it shows 99, so make the PDF first. Change it by hand if the printed book will have more pages than the PDF (for example, extra blank pages or separately printed front matter). Printers usually charge per page, so this has a big effect on the price.

Copies

  • Where: Printers tab › Book & Job Specification
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: Full view only
  • Values: from 1 to 99999, default 50

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

How many copies of the book to be printed.

Explanation:

The number of books to print. All prices, warnings and the total are based on this number. Printing more copies usually lowers the price per copy; use Compare Prices... to see this at 50, 100, 250, 500 and 1000 copies.

Interior

  • Where: Printers tab › Book & Job Specification
  • Type: Drop-down list
  • View level: Full view only
  • Choices: Black & white; Full color

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Whether the inside pages are printed in black & white or full color.

Explanation:

Full color is much more expensive at most printers, even if only a few pages have colour. Choose Black & white unless the inside of the book really needs colour. Some printers do not change the price for colour (Pretore), and some have no colour price data for every size yet (a red note tells you).

Binding

  • Where: Printers tab › Book & Job Specification
  • Type: Drop-down list
  • View level: Full view only
  • Choices: Paperback (soft cover); Hardcover; Saddle-stitched (stapled)

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Preferred binding style. Each printer maps this onto the nearest option it offers.

Explanation:

Paperback is the usual choice. Hardcover costs more but lasts longer. Saddle-stitched (stapled) is only for thin books; printers limit the number of pages (for example Pothi: up to 64 pages). If a printer does not offer your choice, its panel says which binding it priced instead. The binding also changes the Thickness.

Currency

  • Where: Printers tab › Book & Job Specification
  • Type: Drop-down list
  • View level: Full view only

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Currency used to display all quotations and estimates. Prices in other currencies are converted using exchange rates downloaded from the internet (a guide only).

Explanation:

Choose the currency you want to see all prices in. PTXprint converts each printer's prices from its own currency, using exchange rates downloaded from the internet. The conversion is only a guide; the printer will charge in its own currency.

Printers tab

Compare Prices...

  • Where: Printers tab
  • Type: Button
  • View level: Full view only

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Show a graph comparing prices (per copy or total) at several quantities across all the printers ticked in the Compare column above.

Explanation:

Opens the Multi-Quote Comparison graph for every printer ticked in the Compare column. For Pretore, PTXprint first asks Pretore's server for prices (this needs an account and an internet connection). If no ticked printer has a price, no graph appears.

PDF Preview window, layout analysis and page filling

What this window is for

The PDF Preview window shows the PDF that PTXprint has just made. It opens by itself after you click Print. You use it to:

  • read through the pages, one page or two facing pages (a "spread") at a time;
  • find layout problems quickly (for example, pages that are not full, or words with too much space between them);
  • fix small layout problems directly on the page. You right-click a paragraph and make it one line shorter or longer, or you right-click a picture and move it or change its size;
  • run the Auto Page Fill tool, which tries to make every page full by itself.

The Preview window is a separate window. You can keep it open beside the main PTXprint window. Changes that you make in the Preview window are saved with the current configuration.

In this chapter, "pt" means point. One point is about 0.35 mm. "em" is a width equal to the size of the text. For example, in 10 pt text, 1 em is 10 pt.

Opening and closing the Preview window

  • The Preview window opens after each Print, if the main menu (☰) > Show PDF is set to Preview Pane. This is the normal setting. If Show PDF is set to System Viewer, the PDF opens in your normal PDF program instead. If it is set to Output Folder, PTXprint opens the folder that holds the PDF.
  • If you close the Preview window with its X button, it is only hidden. It comes back the next time you print.
  • Click Show main PTXprint settings (shortcut Alt+S) to bring the main window to the front.
  • The title bar shows the PDF file name and the date and time when it was made. Check this to be sure that you are looking at the newest PDF.

The preview has tabs down the left side. Content shows your main PDF. Cover shows the cover PDF, if you made one. Diff shows the comparison PDF, if you used Compare PDFs. Reference shows reference documents such as the Ornaments Catalogue. Tabs without a PDF are hidden.

Moving around: pages, spreads and zoom

The top bar of the window has the navigation controls.

  • First, Previous, Next and Last buttons move through the PDF. In Book View they move by a whole spread.
  • The page box shows the printed page number. Type a number and press Enter to jump to that page.
  • The label next to the page box shows how many pages there are. "(15)+52" means 15 front pages (before page 1) and 52 numbered pages.
  • Keyboard: Left/Right arrow or Page Up/Page Down change page. Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End go to the first and last page.
  • Mouse: turn the mouse wheel to change page. When you are zoomed in, the wheel scrolls the page instead. Hold the middle mouse button and drag to move the page around.
  • Zoom: use the Zoom box, Ctrl+mouse wheel (zooms at the mouse pointer), Ctrl+Plus and Ctrl+Minus. Ctrl+F, Ctrl+0 or the Zoom Fit to Screen button fit the whole page (or spread) in the window.
  • For right-to-left books, the arrow buttons and keys are reversed to follow the direction of the book.

Book View (Ctrl+B) shows two facing pages side by side, as in a printed book. Page 1 is shown alone because it is a right-hand page. Then pages 2+3, 4+5 and so on are shown together. Use Book View to check that facing pages look balanced.

The Contents list on the left shows the bookmarks in the PDF (books, and often chapters). Double-click a line to jump to that page.

The Content tab: what to show on the preview

These options only change what you see in the preview. They do not change the PDF itself.

  • Adjustments draws coloured bars on the edges of paragraphs that have been adjusted. A bar on the left edge means the paragraph was made smaller (shrunk). A bar on the right edge means it was made bigger (expanded). Blue means the number of lines was changed. Red means the text width was changed (the letters were made a little narrower or wider). Red and blue in stripes means both were changed. A thicker bar means a bigger change. Leave this ticked while you work on the layout.
  • Paragraph Boxes draws a thin box around every paragraph that you can adjust. This helps you see where one paragraph ends and the next begins, and where to right-click.
  • Guides and Baselines draws the margins, the header and footer positions and the baselines (the lines on which the text sits). Use it to check that text lines up on the grid.
  • Graph Paper draws a measuring grid over the page. Click Settings next to it to change the units, the number of divisions, the colours and the line thickness.
  • Layout Analysis looks for typesetting problems and marks them in colour on the page. See the next section.

Auto-update

When Auto-update is ticked, PTXprint makes a new PDF by itself a few seconds after you use the right-click menu on the preview. The delay (normally 3 seconds) is shown as "(3.0s delay)". The delay lets you make several changes one after the other. Each new right-click restarts the delay, so only one print is made at the end. Click the delay text to go to the setting in the main window (Advanced tab > Other > Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings > Auto-update Delay (seconds)).

When Auto-update is not ticked, your changes are stored but nothing happens until you click Print (Update PDF) (shortcut Ctrl+P). The right-click menu then also has a Print (Update PDF) item.

Layout Analysis and finding issues

Tick Layout Analysis (on the Content tab, in the Default and Full views) to make PTXprint check the text in the PDF. On a long book this can take some time. A small window says "Analysing text. Press Cancel to stop".

PTXprint can find these kinds of issues. Each is marked on the page with a colour:

Issue What it means Colour on the page
Underfilled Pages A page (or a column) where the text stops before the bottom margin. One or more lines are empty at the foot. (no mark; listed only)
Excessive horizontal whitespace A space between words (or between letters, if letter spacing is turned on) that is wider than the limit. light blue-green bar
Vertical rivers of whitespace Spaces in several lines, one above the other, that form a white "river" running down through the paragraph. yellow
Glyph Collisions Letters or marks that touch or overlap each other, for example a high mark that hits the line above. red
Bad Glyphs A character that the font does not have. It usually prints as an empty box or a question mark. purple

Underfilled pages are always found, even when Layout Analysis is off, because PTXprint learns about them from the typesetting itself. The other four need Layout Analysis.

Note: Layout analysis does not check for widows and orphans (a single line of a paragraph left alone at the top or bottom of a column). You need to look for these yourself.

Locate... and the issue arrows

Click Locate... to choose which kinds of issues the two arrow buttons next to it should find. Locate... is only available when Layout Analysis is ticked.

  • Locate the previous issue and Locate the next issue jump to the previous or next page that has a ticked kind of issue.
  • Hold the mouse over an arrow to see a list of the problem page numbers. The colour of each number shows the kind of issue: red = collisions, light blue = too much space, yellow = rivers, light green = both too much space and rivers, purple = bad glyphs, black = only underfilled. The current page is shown between < and >.
  • The arrows are greyed out when there are no issues in that direction.

The limits that decide what counts as an issue are on the main window: Advanced tab > Other > Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings. Click the Settings link next to Layout Analysis to go there. The most useful one is Bad Space minimum width (em) (normally 1.3). If too many spaces are marked, make it larger. If you set it to 0, PTXprint marks only the worst spaces in the document.

Layout Analysis turns itself off when you change book, configuration or project, and in some other cases. Tick it again when you need it.

Adjusting paragraphs with the right-click menu

PTXprint lets you change how many lines a paragraph uses, without editing the text. This is the main way to fix a page that is too short or too long. It works like this:

  • Lines (blue): PTXprint asks the typesetter to set the paragraph in one line fewer (-1) or one line more (+1). It does this by putting the line breaks in different places. It can only shrink a paragraph if there is enough space in its lines. Short paragraphs often cannot shrink.
  • Text width (red): PTXprint makes the letters of the paragraph a little narrower (for example 98%) or a little wider (for example 102%). This makes it easier to lose or gain a line. Small changes are hard to see. Large changes can be seen, so keep them small.

Right-click on a paragraph in the preview. The first line of the menu shows which paragraph you clicked, for example JHN 3.16 \p +0 100%. This is the book, the verse where the paragraph starts, the paragraph marker, the current line adjustment and the current text width. Then the menu has these items:

Menu item What it does Mouse shortcut
Try Shrink -1 line (or Yes! Shrink -1 line) Asks for one line fewer. The number in brackets is the new line count. Shift + left-click
Shrink Text Makes the letters narrower by one step (normally 1%), down to the limit (normally 95%). Ctrl + left-click
Shrink Both Makes the letters narrower (about half of the room left before the limit) and asks for one line fewer. Ctrl + Shift + left-click
Expand +1 line Asks for one more line. Shift + right-click
Expand Text Makes the letters wider by one step, up to the limit (normally 105%). Ctrl + right-click
Expand Both Makes the letters wider and asks for one more line. Ctrl + Shift + right-click
Reset Adjustments > Paragraph / Column / Page / Spread / End of Book Removes the adjustments from this paragraph, or from all paragraphs in this column, page, spread, or from here to the end of the book. Ctrl or Shift + middle-click resets the paragraph
SpeedSlice Opens the SpeedSlice dialog (see below). Only for \p and \m paragraphs, and not in diglots.
Edit Style \p (or other marker) Opens the Styles tab with this paragraph's style selected.
Jump to Ref in Paratext Shows this verse in Paratext (Windows only).
Zoom to Fit Fits the page in the window (Ctrl+F).
Print (Update PDF) Makes a new PDF now. Only shown when Auto-update is off.

Column only appears in two-column layouts. Spread only appears in Book View when two pages are shown. The step sizes and the limits are on the Advanced tab > Other > Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings (Shrink Text Step Value, Minimum Text Shrink, Expand Text Step Value, Maximum Text Expand).

Notes:

  • The right-click menu only works on paragraphs that PTXprint can link to a verse reference. Right-clicking in the front matter or on a header often shows no menu.
  • A request for -1 line is only a request. If the paragraph cannot lose a line, nothing changes. Then try Shrink Both, or choose a different (longer) paragraph on the same page.
  • Changing one paragraph moves all the text after it. A page that was fine may change. Work from the front of the book to the back.
  • With the mouse shortcuts you can work very fast: Shift+click several paragraphs, wait for the delay, and look at the result.

Where adjustments are stored: the Adj List

Every adjustment is stored in a list for each book, called the Adj List (adjustment list). One row is one paragraph. You can see and edit the list on the main window: View+Edit tab > Adj List. Choose the book at the top of the tab. The columns are:

  • Book and C.V – the book and the chapter.verse where the paragraph starts.
  • Para – which paragraph at that verse (1 = the paragraph that contains the verse, 2 = the next one, for example after a heading).
  • Stretch – the line change (-1, +1, 0 …).
  • Marker – the paragraph marker (for example p or q1).
  • Expand – the text width in percent (100 = normal).
  • Parameters and Comment – extra information. The Auto Page Fill tool writes its measurements here.

The adjustments belong to the current configuration. They are used every time you print with this configuration. The Auto Page Fill tool uses the same list.

How to undo adjustments

There is no Undo button. Use one of these ways:

  • Use the opposite menu item (for example Expand +1 line after Try Shrink -1 line).
  • Right-click the paragraph and choose Reset Adjustments > Paragraph. Or reset a whole Column, Page, Spread or everything to the End of Book.
  • On the View+Edit tab > Adj List, select one or more rows and press Delete (or right-click > Delete Row(s)). You can also click in the Stretch or Expand cell and type a new value.

The change appears in the PDF after the next print.

Moving and resizing pictures with the right-click menu

Right-click on a picture in the preview. The menu shows where the picture is anchored ("Anchored at: MRK 1.10"). An anchor is the verse that the picture is attached to. The menu has:

  • Change Anchor Ref – opens the Enter new anchor verse ref dialog, to attach the picture to a different verse.
  • Frame Size – Column, Span (across both columns), Page or Full (the whole paper). The current choice is marked with ●.
  • Vertical Position – for example Top, Bottom, Center, Before Verse, After Paragraph, Cutout, Below Notes. Only the choices that fit the frame size are shown.
  • Horizontal Position – for example Left, Right, Center, Inner, Outer. Not shown for Span pictures.
  • Mirror Picture – Never, Always, If on odd page or If on even page.
  • Shrink by 1 line / Grow by 1 line – makes the picture smaller or larger by about one line of text in height.
  • Show Details... – opens the Pictures tab with this picture selected, where you can see all its settings.
  • Edit Caption Style \fig – opens the Styles tab at the caption style.

These changes are stored in the picture list (on the Pictures tab), not in the Adj List. If the message "Image Anchor Not Found" appears, PTXprint cannot match the picture to a row in the picture list.

Enter new anchor verse ref (dialog)

Type the new verse in the form JHN 3.16 (book code, space, chapter.verse). The OK button only becomes active when the reference is in the right form, and when there is not already a picture at that verse. A red message explains what is wrong.

SpeedSlice: work on one part of a long book quickly

Each print of a long book (for example Psalms or Isaiah) can take a long time. When you are fixing the layout of pages in the middle of such a book, you must wait for the whole book after every change. SpeedSlice solves this. It tells PTXprint to typeset only a "slice" of the book: it starts at the page you are working on and continues for a few chapters. Then each print is fast.

To open it, right-click on a \p or \m paragraph near the top of the page where you want the slice to begin, and choose SpeedSlice. (It is not available for diglots.) The dialog has:

  • Reference for Start of Slice – filled in from the paragraph you clicked. Either type a chapter (for example JHN 4) to start at the beginning of that chapter, or type the last verse on the page before (for example GEN 3:23).
  • First Word on This Page – if you gave a verse, type the first word that appears on the page where the slice should start. PTXprint skips all the text before that word. The word must be typed exactly as it appears in the text.
  • Slice Marker (usually \m) – the paragraph marker that the slice starts with. Normally \m (a paragraph without a first-line indent), because the page usually starts in the middle of a paragraph.
  • Length of Slice (in chapters) – how many chapters to include (1–10, normally 3).

Click Enable to use the slice. Click Disable to turn it off and go back to printing the whole book.

Important: SpeedSlice stays on until you turn it off. While it is on, your PDF contains only the slice. The page numbers in the slice are not the real page numbers. Always Disable the slice before you make the final PDF.

Auto Page Fill and the progress monitor

The Auto Page Fill tool tries to make every page of every book full, so that the text reaches the bottom margin on every page. It uses the same two methods that you use by hand: it changes the number of lines in some paragraphs and the width of their text. It does not move pictures, and it does not stretch the space between lines. It stores its results in the Adj List, so you can see them and change them later.

The tool does not guess. It really typesets each book many times, and measures the result each time. This takes a lot of computer power and time: from minutes for a short book to hours for a whole Bible. It uses several processor cores at once.

To open the tool, click Show/hide Page Fill tool with progress monitor (the lightning icon) at the top of the Preview window (Default and Full views). The PTXprint: Page Filler window opens. It has one coloured bar for each book that is set to print. It has these buttons:

  • Start Fill – starts filling from the beginning of each book. It starts from no adjustments, so it replaces the adjustments that are already in the Adj List for these books (including the ones you made by hand).
  • Resume Fill – keeps the existing adjustments and continues from the first page in each book that is not full. A book that is already full is marked "Already Filled".
  • Stop! – stops the job. Each book stops after its current test run. This can take a short time.
  • Color Key – shows what each colour of bar means.
  • Settings – opens the settings for the filler on the main window (Advanced tab > Other > Automatic Page Filler).

The bottom of the window shows the time used and how busy the processor is (CPU). The bar colours mean:

Colour Meaning
Grey Not yet started
Grey-blue Probing – first measurements of what each paragraph can do
Sky blue Filling in progress
Tan / light brown Filling in progress, but some pages could not be filled
Green Complete – all pages filled
Orange Incomplete – some pages could not be filled
Red Failed – an error or the time limit was reached
Light yellow Already filled – nothing to do
Peach No page data – the book was skipped and may need attention

When all books have finished, PTXprint makes a new PDF, and the preview shows the result. Then use Locate the next issue (with Underfilled Pages ticked) to find the pages that the tool could not fill, and fix them by hand.

The settings on the Automatic Page Filler group decide how hard the tool tries (speed) and how good the text must look (quality):

  • Time limit for the whole job (minutes) – normally 180.
  • Earlier pages to retry – if a page cannot be filled, the tool goes back this many pages and tries a different layout there (normally 4). Higher = fewer failed pages, but slower. 0 = fastest.
  • Paragraphs to adjust on each page – normally 6. Higher = more pages filled, but each page takes longer.
  • Widest word space allowed (× text size) – normally 1.0. Lower = better-looking text, but more pages may fail.
  • Keep paragraphs close to normal width, Penalise shrink or stretch and Keep neighbouring paragraphs alike – fine control of which changes the tool prefers.

The text width limits come from Minimum Text Shrink and Maximum Text Expand (normally 95% and 105%). The number of books worked on at the same time comes from Maximum parallel processes (Advanced > Other > Page Layout and Spacing).

The buttons at the bottom of the window

  • Show Report Information – makes a report about the current configuration and opens it in your web browser. The button changes colour when the report has warnings or errors, and its tooltip gives a summary.
  • Open the PDF in Default PDF Viewer – opens the PDF in your normal PDF program.
  • Open folder containing the PDF – opens the output folder in your file manager.
  • Save the PDF with a different name – saves a copy of the PDF anywhere you like.
  • Print the PDF on paper – sends the PDF to a printer that is connected to your computer.

Common tasks

Find and fix a page that is not full (manual method)

  1. Print the book. The Preview window opens.
  2. Click Locate... (tick Layout Analysis on the Content tab first if it is greyed out) and make sure Underfilled Pages is ticked.
  3. Click Locate the next issue. The preview jumps to the first page that is not full.
  4. Look at the page (and the page before it). Find a long paragraph whose last line is nearly full. That paragraph can easily gain a line. Or find a paragraph whose last line is very short. That paragraph can easily lose a line.
  5. To pull text up from the next page onto this page, shrink a paragraph on this page or on the page before: Shift + left-click on it (or right-click > Try Shrink -1 line). To push text down, expand a paragraph: Shift + right-click (or Expand +1 line).
  6. Wait for the auto-update (a few seconds). Check the result.
  7. If nothing changed, try Shrink Both, or choose another paragraph. Then click Locate the next issue again.

Make a paragraph one line shorter

  1. Right-click on the paragraph in the preview.
  2. Choose Try Shrink -1 line. The number in brackets is the number of lines you are asking for.
  3. If the paragraph does not get shorter, right-click again and choose Shrink Both (narrower text and one line less).

Remove adjustments that you do not want

  1. Right-click on a paragraph on the page.
  2. Choose Reset Adjustments, then Paragraph, Column, Page, Spread or End of Book.
  3. Or: on the main window, go to View+Edit > Adj List, choose the book, select the rows and press Delete. Then Print.

Fill all pages automatically

  1. On the Basic tab, choose the books that you want to fill.
  2. In the Preview window, click the lightning icon (Show/hide Page Fill tool with progress monitor).
  3. Click Start Fill for a fresh start, or Resume Fill to keep the adjustments that are already there.
  4. Wait. Watch the coloured bars. You can keep using the computer, but it may be slow.
  5. When it has finished, a new PDF appears. Use Locate the next issue to check the pages that could not be filled (orange bars), and fix them by hand.

Check the page for spacing problems, collisions and missing characters

  1. On the Content tab, tick Layout Analysis. Wait for the analysis to finish.
  2. Look for coloured marks on the page: red = collisions, purple = missing characters, yellow = rivers, light blue-green = wide spaces.
  3. Click Locate... and tick only the issue types you want to deal with now.
  4. Use Locate the previous issue and Locate the next issue to go from page to page.

Move a picture or change its size

  1. Right-click on the picture in the preview.
  2. Choose Frame Size, Vertical Position, Horizontal Position or Mirror Picture, and choose the new value. Or choose Shrink by 1 line / Grow by 1 line.
  3. To attach the picture to a different verse, choose Change Anchor Ref, type the new verse (for example MRK 2.4) and click OK.

Work quickly on pages in the middle of a long book

  1. Go to the page you want to work on.
  2. Right-click on a \p or \m paragraph at the top of that page and choose SpeedSlice.
  3. Check the reference. Type the first word on the page in First Word on This Page. Leave Slice Marker as \m. Set Length of Slice (for example 3 chapters).
  4. Click Enable. The next PDF contains only the slice.
  5. Make your adjustments. They are stored in the Adj List and also apply to the full book.
  6. When you have finished, right-click a \p or \m paragraph again, choose SpeedSlice and click Disable. Print again to get the full book.

See two facing pages together

  1. On the Content tab, tick Book View (or press Ctrl+B).
  2. Use the arrows to move one spread at a time.

Common problems

The right-click menu does not appear, or it has no shrink/expand items. The menu needs information that PTXprint writes during printing. Print once with the current configuration. The menu only appears on paragraphs that have a verse reference, so it does not work on most front matter, headers or footers. Right-click on the body text of a paragraph.

I chose "Try Shrink -1 line" but the paragraph did not change. The paragraph has no room to lose a line. This is common for short paragraphs, or when the last line is already nearly full. Try Shrink Both, or shrink a longer paragraph on the same page. Also check that Auto-update is ticked, or click Print (Update PDF).

My changes do not appear in the PDF. If Auto-update is not ticked, you must click Print (Update PDF) (Ctrl+P). If it is ticked, wait for the delay (normally 3 seconds). Each new right-click restarts the delay.

Fixing one page broke another page. Every change moves the text that follows it. Work from the front of the book to the back. Fix the first problem page first, then use Locate the next issue.

The Locate... button and the issue arrows are greyed out. Locate... needs Layout Analysis to be ticked (on the Content tab, Default or Full view). The arrows are greyed out when no issue of a ticked type is found in that direction. Underfilled pages can be found without Layout Analysis.

Layout Analysis has turned itself off. PTXprint turns it off when you change book, configuration or project, and after some other changes (for example one/two columns). Tick it again.

Too many spaces (or almost none) are marked as bad. Change Bad Space minimum width (em) on the Advanced tab > Other > Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings. A larger value marks fewer spaces.

My PDF only has a few chapters, or starts in the middle of the book. SpeedSlice is still enabled. Right-click a \p or \m paragraph, choose SpeedSlice and click Disable. Then print again.

Start Fill removed the adjustments I made by hand. Start Fill starts again from nothing for each book. Use Resume Fill if you want to keep the existing adjustments.

The page filler has been running for a very long time. Filling is slow, especially for long books such as Psalms. You can click Stop!. Pages that are already filled keep their adjustments. To make it faster next time, lower Earlier pages to retry or Paragraphs to adjust on each page in Advanced > Other > Automatic Page Filler.

The text looks squashed or stretched after page filling. Make the range smaller: raise Minimum Text Shrink (for example to 97%) and lower Maximum Text Expand (for example to 103%). Lower Widest word space allowed for less space between words. Then run the fill again. You can also look at the coloured bars (tick Adjustments) to find paragraphs with large changes and reset them.

The Preview window has gone. It was closed or hidden. Print again, or check that the main menu (☰) > Show PDF is set to Preview Pane.

The preview shows an old PDF. Check the date and time in the title bar. If the last print failed, the old PDF is still shown. Look at the message at the bottom of the main window.

Most of the controls described here are missing. Many of them (Layout Analysis, Locate..., the issue arrows, Auto-update, the Auto Page Fill button) only appear in the Default and Full views. Change the view level in the main menu (☰).

Settings reference: PDF Preview window, layout analysis and page filling

Every control in this part of PTXprint is listed below, grouped by where it appears.

PDF Preview > Issue types popup

Bad Glyphs

  • Where: PDF Preview > Issue types popup
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views

Explanation:

Finds pages where the font has no shape for a character. Such characters usually print as an empty box. This is often caused by a wrong font, or by a character that was typed by mistake (for example a wrong Unicode character). Fix it by choosing a font that has the character, or by correcting the text in Paratext. Marked in purple on the page.

Glyph Collisions

  • Where: PDF Preview > Issue types popup
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views

Explanation:

Finds pages where letters or marks touch or overlap, for example a tall diacritic that hits the line above. Marked in red. The sensitivity is controlled by Collision Detection Padding (pt) and Precise collisions on the Advanced tab > Other > Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings. If you find collisions, you may need more line spacing, or a different font.

Excessive horizontal whitespace

  • Where: PDF Preview > Issue types popup
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views

Explanation:

Finds pages with a space between words that is wider than Bad Space minimum width (em) (normally 1.3 em). Wide spaces are common in short lines and in narrow columns. Marked with a light blue-green bar. Hyphenation, a slightly smaller font, or Shrink Text / Expand Text on the paragraph can help.

Vertical rivers of whitespace

  • Where: PDF Preview > Issue types popup
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views

Explanation:

Finds pages with "rivers": spaces in several lines that sit one above the other and make a white stripe down through the text. Marked in yellow. To remove a river, change the line breaks in the paragraph, for example with Shrink Text or Expand Text from the right-click menu.

Underfilled Pages

  • Where: PDF Preview > Issue types popup
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views

Explanation:

Finds pages where a column ends before the bottom margin. This is the most common issue. It is found from the typesetting log, so it works even when Layout Analysis is off. Fix these pages with the right-click shrink/expand items, or with the Auto Page Fill tool. The last page of a book is often short; that is normal.

PDF Preview (dialog)

Zoom

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog)
  • Type: Number box
  • View level: All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)
  • Values: from 10 to 1000, default 100

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Zoom Shortcuts:
Ctrl + F - fit to screen Ctrl + Plus - zoom in Ctrl + Minus - zoom out Ctrl + 0 - fit to screen Ctrl + Scrollwheel - change zoom level

Explanation:

The zoom in percent (100 = actual size). Usually it is easier to use Ctrl+mouse wheel, which zooms at the mouse pointer, or Ctrl+F to fit the page. Values above 800 are limited to 800.

Zoom Fit to Screen

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Zoom Fit to Screen

Explanation:

Fits the whole page, or the whole spread in Book View, in the window. Same as Ctrl+F or Ctrl+0.

Page/Spread

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog)
  • Type: Label
  • View level: All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Shortcuts:
Left-Arrow (or PgUp) - previous page/spread Right-Arrow (or PgDn) - next page/spread Ctrl+Home - First page/spread Ctrl+End - Last page/spread Mouse Scroll also changes pages Ctrl+Mouse Scroll Zooms in/out

Explanation:

Only a label. It shows "Pages:" before the page count. Hold the mouse over it to see the keyboard and mouse shortcuts for moving between pages.

(15)+52

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • Description: First page (or spread)
  • View level: All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

First page (or spread)

Negative page numbers refer to the peripheral pages before the main text begins on Page 1.

Shortcuts:
Left-Arrow (or PgUp) - previous page/spread Right-Arrow (or PgDn) - next page/spread Ctrl+Home - First page/spread Ctrl+End - Last page/spread Mouse Scroll also changes pages Ctrl+Mouse Scroll Zooms in/out

Explanation:

Goes to the first page (or spread). The label next to the page box shows the page count. When it reads like "(15)+52", the number in brackets is the number of pages before page 1 (for example title page and contents), and the second number is the number of numbered pages.

Previous page (or spread)

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • View level: All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Previous page (or spread)

Explanation:

Goes back one page, or one spread in Book View. Same as Left arrow or Page Up. In a right-to-left book the direction is reversed.

Type page number to jump to

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog)
  • Type: Text box
  • View level: All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Type page number to jump to.

Shortcuts:
Left-Arrow (or PgUp) - previous page/spread Right-Arrow (or PgDn) - next page/spread Ctrl+Home - First page/spread Ctrl+End - Last page/spread Mouse Scroll also changes pages Ctrl+Mouse Scroll Zooms in/out

Explanation:

Shows the current page number and lets you jump to a page. Type the printed page number (the number on the page, not the position in the PDF file) and press Enter. If that page number does not exist, the preview goes to the nearest page.

Next page (or spread)

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • View level: All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)
