Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Next page (or spread)

Explanation:

Goes forward one page, or one spread in Book View. Same as Right arrow or Page Down.

Last page (or spread)

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • View level: All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Last page (or spread)

Explanation:

Goes to the last page (or spread). Same as Ctrl+End.

Locate...

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog)
  • Type: Menu button
  • Description: Select which types of issues to highlight
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Layout Analysis” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

The next/previous issue arrows will jump to pages with issues to be resolved. You can choose which kinds of issues to deal with.

Note: It is only enabled when Layout Analysis is active. Without it, the arrows only jump to underfilled pages.

Explanation:

Opens a small list where you tick which kinds of issues the two arrow buttons should find: Bad Glyphs, Glyph Collisions, Excessive horizontal whitespace, Vertical rivers of whitespace and Underfilled Pages. Tick only the kinds you want to work on now. Greyed out until Layout Analysis is ticked.

Locate the previous issue

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Locate previous page with issues.

Explanation:

Jumps to the previous page that has an issue of a ticked kind. Hold the mouse over the button to see the list of problem pages, coloured by kind of issue.

Locate the next issue

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Locate next page with issues.

Explanation:

Jumps to the next page that has an issue of a ticked kind. This is the button you will use most when fixing the layout: fix a page, then click this to go to the next problem. Hold the mouse over the button to see the list of problem pages.

Print (Update PDF)

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • View level: All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Update the PDF

Shortcut: Ctrl-P

Explanation:

Makes a new PDF with the current settings and adjustments. It is the same as Print on the main window. Shortcut: Ctrl+P. You need it when Auto-update is off, or after you change settings on the main window.

Show/hide the Page Filler with progress monitor

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog)
  • Type: Toggle button (not ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Show/hide the Page Filler with progress monitor

Explanation:

Shows or hides the PTXprint: Page Filler window (the Auto Page Fill tool and its progress monitor). Opening the window does not start anything. You start the job with Start Fill or Resume Fill in that window. The job can take a long time and uses a lot of processor power.

Show main PTXprint settings

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • View level: All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Show the main PTXprint dialog with all the settings. Shortcut: Alt+S

Explanation:

Brings the main PTXprint window to the front, so that you can change settings. Shortcut: Alt+S.

Show Report Information

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Display a report on the current configuration.

Explanation:

Makes a report on the current configuration and opens it in your web browser. The report lists possible problems, for example the number of underfilled pages. The button changes colour when there are warnings or errors, and its tooltip then gives a short summary.

Open the PDF in Default PDF Viewer

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • View level: All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Open the PDF in the system's default PDF viewer (e.g. Evince, Acrobat or SumatraPDF).

Explanation:

Opens the PDF in the PDF program that your computer normally uses. Use it when you want to search the text or print with that program.

Preview Pane: Open folder containing the PDF

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • View level: All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Open the folder which contains the PDF file(s) created for this project.

Explanation:

Opens the folder where PTXprint saves the PDF files for this project. Use it to find the PDF to send to someone.

Save the PDF with a different name

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • View level: All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Save a COPY of this PDF with a new name and/or different folder.

Explanation:

Saves a copy of the PDF with a new name or in a different folder. The original PDF stays where it is. PTXprint remembers the last folder you used.

Print the PDF on paper

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • View level: All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Print the PDF on paper using a physical printer connected to this device.

Explanation:

Prints the PDF on a printer connected to your computer. This is for proof copies. For the final book, send the PDF to the printing company.

PDF Preview (dialog) › Content tab

Auto-update

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog) › Content tab
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

When enabled, this re-creates the PDF after making changes using the (right-click) context menu options.

Note that there is a short delay enabling you to make several adjustments one after the other before the update is triggered. This delay can be adjusted by clicking on the value shown here or refer to: Advanced > Other > Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings.

Explanation:

When ticked, PTXprint makes a new PDF by itself a short time after you use the right-click menu on the preview (shrink, expand, reset, picture changes and so on). Ticking it also starts an update straight away. When it is not ticked, your changes are stored, and you click Print (Update PDF) when you are ready. Untick it if each print takes a long time and you want to make many changes first.

(3.0s delay)

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog) › Content tab
  • Type: EventBox
  • View level: All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

When enabled, this re-creates the PDF after making changes using the (right-click) context menu options.

Note that there is a short delay enabling you to make several adjustments one after the other before the update is triggered. This delay can be adjusted by clicking on the value shown here or refer to: Advanced > Other > Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings.

(3.0s delay)

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog) › Content tab
  • Type: Label
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

When enabled, this re-creates the PDF after making changes using the (right-click) context menu options.

Note that there is a short delay enabling you to make several adjustments one after the other before the update is triggered. This delay can be adjusted by clicking on the value shown here or refer to: Advanced > Other > Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings.

Explanation:

Shows how many seconds PTXprint waits after your last right-click change before it makes a new PDF. Click it to go to the Auto-update Delay (seconds) setting on the Advanced tab > Other > Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings. Make the delay longer if the print starts before you have finished your changes.

Book View

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog) › Content tab
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • View level: All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Toggle between a single page view and a book (spread) view. Shortcut: Ctrl + B

Explanation:

Shows two facing pages side by side, like an open book (shortcut Ctrl+B). Page 1 is shown alone. Use it to check that facing pages look balanced and end at the same height. Untick it to see one page at a time, which gives a larger view.

Adjustments

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog) › Content tab
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • View level: All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Show color-coded lines on the left and right edges of paragraphs to indicate the kind of shrink or stretch that has been applied as well as the amount (thickness of line).

These adjustment annotations are not part of the PDF, but are only overlaid on the text to help refine the layout.

Key:

Left=shrink Right=expand

blue=shrink/expand lines red=shrink/expand text

Interleaved red+blue indicates that both lines and text have been shrunk (or both expanded).

Explanation:

Draws coloured bars on the edges of adjusted paragraphs. Left edge = shrunk, right edge = expanded. Blue = number of lines changed, red = text width changed. A thicker bar means a bigger change. The bars are only in the preview, never in the PDF. Use this to see quickly which paragraphs have been adjusted by you or by the Auto Page Fill tool.

Paragraph Boxes

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog) › Content tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • Description: Show Paragraph Boxes
  • View level: All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Draw boxes around the boundaries of all adjustable paragraphs.

Explanation:

Draws a thin box around each paragraph that you can adjust. This shows you where each paragraph starts and ends, so you know where to right-click. Shown only in the preview.

Guides and Baselines

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog) › Content tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • Description: Show guides and baselines
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

This option displays various guides (showing margins, headers and footers) as well as the baselines of the body text.

Explanation:

Draws guide lines on the preview: the margins, the header and footer positions, and the baselines of the body text. Use it to check that the text sits on the line grid and that headers and footers are in the right place.

Graph Paper

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog) › Content tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • Description: Show grid (graph paper)
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

If the standard Rules and Guides are inadequate you can generate a graph-paper-like grid behind the text. This may be useful for precise measuring.

Explanation:

Draws a graph-paper grid over the preview page. Use it to measure positions and sizes, for example of pictures or margins. Click Settings next to it to change the grid.

Settings

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog) › Content tab
  • Type: Label
  • Description: Graph Paper Settings
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Change the graph paper settings.

Explanation:

Opens the Change the Grid Settings dialog. There you can set the grid units, divisions, offset, colours and line thickness for Graph Paper.

Layout Analysis

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog) › Content tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • Description: Perform Layout Analysis of the text to highlight issues
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

This option analyzes the text to highlight layout issues:
- character collisions
- missing glyphs (bad glyphs)
- excessive horizontal space
- vertical rivers of space

Explanation:

Checks the text of the PDF for typesetting problems and marks them on the page: wide spaces, rivers, collisions and missing characters (bad glyphs). It also makes the Locate... button available. The check takes some time on large PDFs. It is done again after each print while it is ticked. It turns itself off when you change book or configuration.

Settings

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog) › Content tab
  • Type: Label
  • Description: Layout Analysis Settings
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Click to show the Advanced > Other settings to adjust the parameters which control what should get highlighted as an issue.

Explanation:

Opens the main window at the Advanced tab > Other > Preview Pane: Adjustment and Analysis Settings. There you set the limits that decide what is marked as an issue, for example Bad Space minimum width (em) and the river detection settings.

Contents

  • Where: PDF Preview (dialog) › Content tab
  • Type: Table
  • View level: All view levels (Mini, Basic, Default, Full)

Explanation:

Lists the bookmarks in the PDF, usually the books and often the chapters. Double-click a line to jump to that page. If there is only one book, its list is opened out automatically.

Enter new anchor verse ref (dialog)

OK

  • Where: Enter new anchor verse ref (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • View level: Default and Full views

Explanation:

Moves the picture to the new anchor verse and updates the picture list. It is only active when the reference is valid and no other picture uses that verse.

Cancel

  • Where: Enter new anchor verse ref (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • View level: Default and Full views

Explanation:

Closes the dialog without changing the anchor.

Anchor Ref

  • Where: Enter new anchor verse ref (dialog)
  • Type: Text box
  • Description: Enter a new anchor verse
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Enter the new anchor verse reference (e.g. JHN 3.16)

Explanation:

Type the verse that the picture should be attached to, in the form JHN 3.16 (book code, a space, chapter.verse). A colon is changed to a full stop for you. For a diglot, the book code can include the side letter (for example JHNR 3.16). The picture then appears near that verse.

SpeedSlice (dialog)

Enable

  • Where: SpeedSlice (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Print only this slice of the book (for quick layout work).

Explanation:

Turns SpeedSlice on with the values in the dialog. The next print contains only the slice. Remember to turn it off before you make the final PDF.

Disable

  • Where: SpeedSlice (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Turn SpeedSlice off, so that the whole book is printed next time.

Explanation:

Turns SpeedSlice off. The next print contains the whole book again. Use this when you have finished working on the slice.

Reference for Start of Slice

  • Where: SpeedSlice (dialog)
  • Type: Text box
  • Description: Slice Dialog: Enter reference to begin SpeedSlice
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Either enter a chapter number to begin with (e.g. JHN 4) or enter the last verse on the preceding page (e.g. GEN 3:23) to begin the slice. Previous content will be skipped over.

SpeedSlice stays on until you click Disable in this dialog.

Explanation:

Where the slice starts. It is filled in from the paragraph you right-clicked. Type a chapter only (for example PSA 45) to start at the start of that chapter. Or type the last verse on the previous page (for example GEN 3:23); then you must also fill in First Word on This Page.

First Word on This Page

  • Where: SpeedSlice (dialog)
  • Type: Text box
  • Description: Slice Dialog: Enter first word on page
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Enter the first word on this page (where the Slice will begin).

Explanation:

The first word on the page where the slice should begin. PTXprint looks for this word after the verse in Reference for Start of Slice and skips everything before it. Type it exactly as it appears in the text (same spelling and letters). If the word is not found, the slice cannot start at that place.

Slice Marker (usually \m)

  • Where: SpeedSlice (dialog)
  • Type: Text box
  • Description: Slice Dialog: Enter beginning marker
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

What USFM marker needs to be used at the beginning of the Slice? (almost always \m)

Explanation:

The paragraph marker that PTXprint puts at the start of the slice. Use \m in almost all cases. \m is a paragraph with no first-line indent, which matches a page that starts in the middle of a paragraph.

Length of Slice (in chapters)

  • Where: SpeedSlice (dialog)
  • Type: Number box
  • Description: Slice Dialog: Length of Slice
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Values: from 1 to 10, default 3

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Roughly how many chapters should the Slice contain?

Explanation:

How many chapters the slice contains (1 to 10). A short slice prints faster. Make it long enough to include all the pages you want to work on. In books with long chapters, 1 or 2 chapters may be enough.

Importing settings

What this dialog is for

The Import Settings dialog copies settings from somewhere else into a configuration. Use it when:

  • you have a PDF that PTXprint made earlier, and you want the same layout again (for example, the settings were lost, or the PDF came from another person),
  • someone sent you a PTXprint ZIP archive,
  • another project or configuration has settings that you want to reuse – all of them, or only some groups (for example only the pictures, or only the header and footer).

You can also use it to extract the settings from a PDF or ZIP into a normal folder, so that you can look at them.

To open the dialog: on the Basic tab, in the Layout Configuration area, click Import Settings.... (This button is not shown in the Mini view.)

The dialog has three parts: Source of Settings (where the settings come from), Target (where they go), and a row of category tabs (what to bring in).

Source of Settings

Choose one of two sources:

  • PDF file (with embedded settings) or ZIP archive file – click Select... and choose the file.
    • A PDF only works if it was made by PTXprint with Include Config Settings Within PDF turned on (on the Finishing tab). Otherwise PTXprint says that it cannot find any settings in the file.
    • A ZIP archive is the kind of file that PTXprint makes with Create Archive... on the Help tab.
  • A Previously Saved Configuration – choose the Project and then the Configuration to copy from. Settings are read from the saved files, so if the source is the configuration that is open now, click Save first.

Target

Choose where the settings go:

  • A New/Existing Project and/or Configuration – this is the usual choice. PTXprint fills in the current project and configuration. You can choose another existing project. You can choose another configuration, or type a new configuration name. A new configuration starts with the PTXprint default settings, and then the imported settings are added.
  • An External Folder of Settings – click Select... and choose a folder. PTXprint copies all the settings files from the source into that folder. Nothing in your projects is changed. When this target is chosen, Everything is turned on and the category tabs are greyed out.

The OK button stays greyed out until the choices are complete: a file or a source configuration, a target folder or a target configuration, and at least one category ticked. It is also greyed out when the source and the target are the same configuration.

What to import: the category tabs

Each tab has a check box in its label. Tick the box to import that group. Click the tab to see its options.

  • Pictures – the picture settings and the picture list.
  • Layout – the page and column layout.
  • Fonts+Script – fonts and writing-system settings.
  • Styles – the style settings from the Styles tab.
  • Other – a list of other groups that you choose one by one.
  • Everything – all settings. (Only shown in the Default and Full views.)

When Everything is ticked, PTXprint imports everything, no matter which other boxes are ticked or not ticked. Untick Everything if you want only some groups.

What each category brings in

Category What is imported
Pictures The general settings of the Pictures tab (include pictures, picture folder, resolution, captions shown, placeholders…) and the picture list. With Import Entire PicList "as is" the whole list is replaced. With Import Elements of PicList only the parts you tick are copied for each picture.
Layout Page size, margins (top, bottom, side), mirror pages and binding gutter, number of columns and column gutter, vertical rule between columns, line spacing, note lines, margin notes, and related settings. It does not bring the font size (that is in Fonts+Script) or the header and footer (that is in Other › Header+Footer settings).
Fonts+Script The main fonts (regular, bold, italic, bold italic, extra), the font size, the fallback font, text direction, script and line-breaking settings, word and letter spacing, coloured text, and script-specific options. Fonts that are set inside individual styles are not changed.
Styles The style settings from the source (the Styles tab). Normally only styles that you have not changed in the target are updated. Tick Override ALL Style Settings to update all styles.
Other Only the groups that you tick on the Other tab (see below).
Everything All settings in the source configuration, including the book list, copyright text, diglot and Strong's settings, the whole picture list, styles, front matter, cover, and the special files from the Advanced tab.

The Other tab

  • Body Tab settings – the settings on the Body tab, including hyphenation, chapter and verse numbers, section headings, and glossary markup.
  • Notes+Refs settings – footnotes, cross-references and study notes.
  • Header+Footer settings – the content and position of the header and footer.
  • Thumb Tabs settings – the thumb tab settings from the Tabs+Borders tab.
  • Advanced settings – the options on the Advanced tab, and the special files that go with them (changes file, extra TeX files, extra style file, and a custom script if the source uses one).
  • Cover settings – the cover settings, cover styles and cover pages.
  • Front +Back Matter – most settings of the Peripherals tab (front and back PDFs, table of contents, front matter, section introductions), the front matter text, and any variables that the target does not have yet.
  • Overwrite Front Matter – (only available when Front +Back Matter or Cover settings is ticked) replace the existing front matter in the target, not only add missing parts.
  • Custom Script – the custom script processing set on the Advanced tab. Greyed out when the source is a PDF, because a PDF does not contain the script.
  • Borders + Decorations – page borders, section-heading decorations, end-of-book and verse-number decorations. (Default and Full views.)
  • Variables + Meta Data – the variables from the Peripherals tab and other information about the publication. (Default and Full views.)
  • Texpert Hacks – the expert TeX settings on the Advanced tab. (Default and Full views.)
  • Finishing settings – everything on the Finishing tab: PDF output format, watermark, crop marks, grid, pages per sheet, compare-PDF settings and similar. (Default and Full views.)

What happens when you click OK

  1. PTXprint reads the settings from the source.
  2. It changes only the groups you ticked, in the target configuration.
  3. It saves the target configuration at once.
  4. It opens the target project and configuration, and shows a message such as "Imported Settings into: ABC::NT_A5".

There is no Undo. If you are not sure, import into a new configuration name first, and check the result there.

RESET

The RESET button at the bottom of the dialog sets all settings of the current configuration back to the PTXprint defaults. It does not reset the style settings. The dialog stays open, and nothing is saved until you click Save or Print (Make PDF) (or until an import saves the configuration). Use it when you want the target to have only the imported settings, for example before you import styles.

Common tasks

Get back the settings that were used for a PDF

  1. On the Basic tab, click Import Settings....
  2. Click PDF file (with embedded settings) or ZIP archive file, then Select..., and choose the PDF.
  3. Under Target, click A New/Existing Project and/or Configuration. In Configuration, type a new name, for example FromPDF.
  4. Tick Everything (change to the Default view if you cannot see it).
  5. Click OK. PTXprint opens the new configuration with the settings from the PDF.

Copy only the pictures from another configuration

  1. Click Import Settings....
  2. Click A Previously Saved Configuration and choose the source Project and Configuration.
  3. Check that the Target is the configuration you want.
  4. Untick Everything, Layout, Fonts+Script, Styles and Other. Tick Pictures.
  5. On the Pictures tab, choose Import Entire PicList "as is", or choose Import Elements of PicList and tick only what you want (for example Size, Position, Mirror, Rotation settings).
  6. Click OK.

Copy the header and footer from another configuration

  1. Click Import Settings... and choose the source configuration.
  2. Untick Everything and all other categories, and tick Other.
  3. On the Other tab, untick everything except Header+Footer settings.
  4. Click OK.

Look at the settings inside a PDF or ZIP without changing anything

  1. Click Import Settings... and choose the PDF or ZIP file as the source.
  2. Under Target, click An External Folder of Settings, then Select..., and choose an empty folder.
  3. Click OK. The settings files are copied into that folder.

Start a configuration again from defaults, then import styles

  1. Open the configuration on the Basic tab.
  2. Click Import Settings..., then RESET.
  3. Choose the source, untick Everything, and tick Styles (and other groups you need).
  4. Click OK.

Common problems

"Cannot find any settings to import from the selected file"

Cause: The PDF was made without Include Config Settings Within PDF (on the Finishing tab), or with a very old PTXprint version (before 2.3). What to do: Use another source, for example a ZIP archive made with Create Archive... on the Help tab.

The OK button is greyed out

Cause: Something is missing: no file selected, no target folder, no target configuration, no category ticked – or the source and target are the same configuration. What to do: Check each part of the dialog.

Everything was imported, but I ticked only one category

Cause: Everything was still ticked. In the Basic view the Everything tab is hidden, but it is still ticked (it is ticked by default). What to do: Change to the Default view (☰ › View Level › Default View) and untick Everything.

The styles did not change

Cause: Without Override ALL Style Settings, PTXprint only updates styles that are still unchanged in the target. What to do: Tick Override ALL Style Settings, or click RESET before you import.

The font size did not change when I imported Layout

Cause: The font size belongs to Fonts+Script, not Layout. What to do: Tick Fonts+Script too.

The header and footer did not change when I imported Layout

Cause: The header and footer belong to Other › Header+Footer settings. What to do: Tick Other and Header+Footer settings.

Custom Script is greyed out

Cause: The source is a PDF. A PDF does not contain the custom script. What to do: Import from a ZIP archive or a saved configuration instead.

Some options on the Other tab seem to have no effect

Cause: In the current version, Thumb Tabs settings, Overwrite Front Matter, Variables + Meta Data and Custom Script may not bring in their settings when they are used on their own. What to do: After importing, check the Tabs+Borders, Peripherals and Advanced tabs. If something is missing, import into a new configuration with Everything ticked, or set those few settings by hand.

Settings reference: Importing settings

Every control in this part of PTXprint is listed below, grouped by where it appears.

Import Settings... (dialog)

RESET

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • Description: Reset the current Configuration's UI settings
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Warning! This will reset ALL the UI settings for the CURRENT configuration to their default values.

Note that it will NOT reset the Style settings stored in the .sty files.

The reset is not saved until you next save, print, or import with OK.

Explanation:

Sets every setting of the configuration that is open now back to the PTXprint defaults, at once and without asking. Style settings are not reset. The change is not saved until you click Save, Print (Make PDF), or OK to import.

OK

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views

Explanation:

Imports the ticked groups into the target, saves the target configuration, and opens it. With an external folder as target, it copies the settings files into the folder instead. Greyed out until the choices are complete. Shortcut: Alt+Enter.

Cancel

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog)
  • Type: Button
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views

Explanation:

Closes the dialog without importing. (Changes made with RESET stay on the screen.) Shortcut: Ctrl+W.

Pictures

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog)
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • Description: Import Picture Settings
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Everything” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Import the picture settings and the picture list. Use the Pictures tab of this dialog to choose how the picture list is combined.

Explanation:

Imports the general picture settings (from the Pictures tab) and the picture list. The options on the Pictures tab of this dialog control how the picture list is combined. When you tick or untick this box, the Pictures tab of the dialog opens.

Layout

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog)
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • Description: Import Layout Settings
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Everything” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Import page size, margins, columns, line spacing and related settings.

Explanation:

Imports the page layout: page size, margins, gutters, columns, line spacing and similar. It does not import font size, fonts, or the header and footer. The text on the Layout tab of the dialog also mentions the header and footer, but they are imported with Other › Header+Footer settings.

Fonts+Script

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog)
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • Description: Import Fonts and Script Settings
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Everything” is selected

Explanation:

Imports the main fonts, the font size, and the writing-system settings (text direction, script, line breaking, spacing, fallback font, coloured text). Fonts that are set inside individual styles are not changed. Hyphenation settings are imported with Other › Body Tab settings, not here.

Styles

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog)
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • Description: Import Styles Settings
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Everything” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Import the style settings (Styles tab), merged into the target configuration.

Explanation:

Imports the style settings (the Styles tab) by merging them into the target. Only styles that are unchanged in the target are updated, unless Override ALL Style Settings is ticked. Font names and font features inside styles are only imported when Everything is ticked.

Other

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog)
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • Description: Import Other Settings
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Everything” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Use the Other tab of this dialog to choose more groups of settings. If this is not ticked, none of the boxes on the Other tab are used.

Explanation:

Turns on the Other tab, where you choose more groups one by one (Body, Notes+Refs, Header+Footer, Advanced, Cover, Front +Back Matter, Finishing…). If this box is not ticked, none of the boxes on the Other tab are used.

Everything

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog)
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • Description: Import All Settings
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Import all settings and files of the source configuration, whatever the other boxes say.

Explanation:

Imports all settings and files of the source configuration, whatever the other boxes say. Use it to recreate a configuration from a PDF or ZIP, or to make a full copy. It is ticked by default, and PTXprint ticks it again when you open the dialog with no category ticked. It is also turned on automatically when the target is an external folder. Only shown in the Default and Full views – in the Basic view it is hidden but still works.

Import Settings... (dialog) › Source of Settings

PDF file (with embedded settings) or ZIP archive file

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Source of Settings
  • Type: Radio button
  • Description: Import: From existing PDF file or ZIP archive
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

It is possible to import settings from an existing PDF file which was produced earlier by PTXprint. But this only works if the settings are embedded within the PDF. (This is enabled on the Finishing tab).

Importing from a PTXprint ZIP archive (created on the Help tab) is also possible.

Explanation:

Import from a PDF made by PTXprint (with settings embedded) or from a PTXprint ZIP archive. Click Select... to choose the file.

A Previously Saved Configuration

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Source of Settings
  • Type: Radio button
  • Description: Import: From Saved Configuration
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views

Explanation:

Import from a configuration that is saved on this computer. Choose the Project and Configuration below. Choosing a project or configuration in those lists also selects this option.

Project

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Source of Settings
  • Type: Drop-down list
  • Description: Import: Project name
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Choices: unknown
  • Only available when: “A Previously Saved Configuration” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Select the project from which the settings will be imported.

Explanation:

The project that has the configuration you want to copy from. When you choose a project, the Configuration list is filled with its configurations, and Default is selected.

Configuration

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Source of Settings
  • Type: Drop-down list
  • Description: Import: Project configuration
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Choices: (None)
  • Only available when: “A Previously Saved Configuration” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Select a configuration from the selected project from which the settings will be imported.

Explanation:

The configuration to copy settings from. The settings are read from the saved files, so save the source configuration first if it is open.

Select...

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Source of Settings
  • Type: Button
  • Description: Select PDF to import settings from
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “PDF file (with embedded settings) or ZIP archive file” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Select either a PTXprint PDF or ZIP archive to import the settings from.

Importing from a PDF will only work if the PDF contains the PTXprint configuration settings (as enabled on the Finishing tab).

Explanation:

Opens a file chooser, starting in the output folder of the current project, where PTXprint keeps its PDFs. Choose a PDF or ZIP. If the file has no PTXprint settings, PTXprint shows an error and changes back to A Previously Saved Configuration. The chosen file name is shown next to the button.

Import Settings... (dialog) › Target

An External Folder of Settings

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Target
  • Type: Radio button
  • Description: Extract settings to an external folder
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Settings can be extracted to an external folder.

This may be useful when examining settings from a different user, or when there is a need to recover lost settings from a known good PDF or Zip archive.

Explanation:

Copy the settings files to a folder instead of into a configuration. No project is changed. This is useful to look at someone else's settings, or to rescue a few files from a good PDF or ZIP. Everything is used automatically.

A New/Existing Project and/or Configuration

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Target
  • Type: Radio button
  • Description: Import: Into Project/Configuration
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views

Explanation:

Import into a configuration of a project on this computer. This is the usual choice. The current project and configuration are filled in when the dialog opens.

Project

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Target
  • Type: Drop-down list
  • Description: Import: Project name
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Choices: unknown
  • Only available when: “A New/Existing Project and/or Configuration” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Select an existing project into which the settings will be imported.
OR Enter a NEW project name which causes a (temporary) project to be created in the normal Paratext folder.

Select the project into which the settings will be imported.

Explanation:

The project that receives the settings. Choose one of your existing projects. Choosing a project here also selects A New/Existing Project and/or Configuration and fills the Configuration list.

Select...

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Target
  • Type: Button
  • Description: Select target folder for extracted settings
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “An External Folder of Settings” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Select a folder to save the settings in. This could be in a temporary location from where just the needed settings can be accessed and copied into the appropriate place of an existing config.

Explanation:

Opens a folder chooser for An External Folder of Settings. Choose an empty folder, so that the extracted files are easy to find. The chosen folder is shown next to the button.

Configuration

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Target
  • Type: Drop-down list
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Choices: Default
  • Only available when: “A New/Existing Project and/or Configuration” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Choose a configuration from the selected project into which the settings will be imported.
OR Enter a NEW config name which causes a new configuration to be created for the current/new project.

Select a configuration in the selected project into which the settings will be imported.

Explanation:

The configuration that receives the settings. Choose an existing one, or type a new name to create a new configuration. Importing into a new configuration is the safest way to try an import, because your existing configurations are not changed.

Enter a name for the configuration to be saved.

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Target
  • Type: Text box
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “A New/Existing Project and/or Configuration” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Enter a name for the configuration to be saved.

Note that only Roman/Latin names are supported using: a-z A-Z, 0-9, parentheses, underscores and hyphens.

Explanation:

The text part of the target Configuration box. Type a new configuration name here. Use only letters a–z and A–Z, numbers, (, ), _ and -, with no spaces. A new configuration starts from the PTXprint defaults, so tick Everything (or all the groups you need).

Import Settings... (dialog) › Pictures tab

Import Entire PicList "as is" (overwrite existing PicList)

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Pictures tab
  • Type: Radio button
  • Description: Import: Entire PicList "as is" (overwrite existing PicList)
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Pictures” is selected

Explanation:

Replaces the target's whole picture list with the source's picture list. Pictures that were only in the target are removed. Use it when the source is the "master" picture list. (Default and Full views.)

Import Elements of PicList (preserving existing PicList)

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Pictures tab
  • Type: Radio button
  • Description: Import: Elements of PicList (preserving existing PicList)
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Pictures” is selected

Explanation:

Keeps the target's picture list, and copies only the parts you tick below (captions, size and position, copyright) for pictures that are in both lists. Use Add Any New Pictures and Remove Any Old Pictures to control which pictures are in the list. (Default and Full views.)

Captions

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Pictures tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Import Elements of PicList (preserving existing PicList)”, “Pictures” is selected

Explanation:

Copies the caption text, the caption of the second text in a diglot, and the reference shown with the picture. Leave it unticked if the target is in another language, because the captions would then be in the wrong language.

Size, Position, Mirror, Rotation settings

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Pictures tab
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Import Elements of PicList (preserving existing PicList)”, “Pictures” is selected

Explanation:

Copies the size, the position on the page, the scale, mirroring and rotation of each picture. This is useful when two projects share the same pictures and layout.

Copyright Information

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Pictures tab
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Import Elements of PicList (preserving existing PicList)”, “Pictures” is selected

Explanation:

Copies the copyright (credit) information of each picture.

Add Any New Pictures

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Pictures tab
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Pictures” is selected

Explanation:

Adds pictures that are in the source list but not yet in the target list. Leave it ticked unless you want to keep exactly the pictures that the target already has.

Remove Any Old Pictures

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Pictures tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Pictures” is selected

Explanation:

Removes pictures from the target list that are not in the source list. Tick it when the source list is the complete, final list.

Import Settings... (dialog) › Styles tab

Override ALL Style Settings

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Styles tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Normally only styles that have not been changed in the receiving configuration will be imported. But if you require ALL styles to be updated regardless of whether they have already been modified locally, then enable this option.

Explanation:

Normally, PTXprint only updates styles that you have not changed in the target, so your own style changes are kept. Tick this box to update all styles from the source, even the ones you changed.

Import Settings... (dialog) › Other tab

Body Tab settings

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Other tab
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)

  • Only available when: “Other” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Import the settings of the Body tab.

Explanation:

Imports the settings of the Body tab: how books and chapters start, chapter and verse numbers, section headings, hyphenation, glossary markup, and similar.

Notes+Refs settings

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Other tab
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Other” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Import the settings of the Notes+Refs tab.

Explanation:

Imports the settings of the Notes+Refs tab: footnotes, cross-references, note callers, note rules and study notes.

Header+Footer settings

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Other tab
  • Type: Checkbox (ticked by default)
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Other” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Import the settings of the Header+Footer tab.

Explanation:

Imports the settings of the Header+Footer tab: what is shown in the header and footer, and the header and footer positions.

Thumb Tabs settings

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Other tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Other” is selected

Explanation:

Meant to import the thumb tab settings from the Tabs+Borders tab. In the current version it may not bring in these settings; after importing, check the Tabs+Borders tab.

Overwrite Front Matter

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Other tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Front +Back Matter”, “Cover settings”, “Other” is selected

Explanation:

Only available when Front +Back Matter or Cover settings is ticked. It is meant to replace the front matter in the target with the source's front matter, instead of only adding missing parts. In the current version it may have no effect unless Everything is ticked; check the front matter on the Peripherals tab after importing.

Advanced settings

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Other tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Other” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

This includes everything on the Advanced tab with the exception of Custom Script processing and Customized Styles (custom.sty).

Explanation:

Imports the options of the Advanced tab and the files that go with them: the changes file, the extra TeX files, and the extra style file (merged with the target's). If the source uses a custom script and the script file is in the source, it is copied too. The customized styles file (custom.sty) is not imported.

Cover settings

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Other tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Other” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Import the cover settings, cover styles and the cover pages of the front matter.

Explanation:

Imports the cover settings, the cover styles, and the cover pages from the source's front matter. It also turns on decorations, which the cover uses.

Front +Back Matter

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Other tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Other” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

This includes most of the settings on the Peripherals tab, but not the Variables and Values. Front Matter and also Section Introductions are included in this.

Explanation:

Imports the settings of the Peripherals tab (front and back PDFs, table of contents, front matter, colophon, section introductions), the front matter pages from the source, and any variables that the target does not have yet. Existing variable values in the target are not changed.

Custom Script

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Other tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Other” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

This includes the Custom Script processing defined on the Advanced tab.

Note that it is not possible to extract a custom script from a PDF file, which is why this option is sometimes disabled.

Explanation:

Meant for the custom script set on the Advanced tab. Greyed out when the source is a PDF, because a PDF does not hold the script. In the current version the script is imported together with Advanced settings, so tick that box as well.

Borders + Decorations

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Other tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Other” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

This includes the various decorative borders and other ornamental features including section headers, end-of-book and verse number decorators.

Explanation:

Imports the decoration settings from the Tabs+Borders tab: page borders, section-heading decorations, the book-title border, end-of-book decorations and verse-number decorations. (Default and Full views.)

Variables + Meta Data

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Other tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Other” is selected

Explanation:

Meant to import the variables (the values on the Peripherals tab) and information about the publication. In the current version it may have no effect on its own; variables that the target is missing are also added by Front +Back Matter. (Default and Full views.)

Texpert Hacks

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Other tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Other” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Import the expert TeX (TeXpert) settings.

Explanation:

Imports the expert TeX settings (the "TeXpert" options on the Advanced tab). Use it only if you know that the source used special TeX settings. (Default and Full views.)

Finishing settings

  • Where: Import Settings... (dialog) › Other tab
  • Type: Checkbox (not ticked by default)
  • View level: Default and Full views
  • Only available when: “Other” is selected

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

This includes everything on the Finishing tab.

Explanation:

Imports the settings of the Finishing tab: PDF output format, watermark, crop marks, grid, pages per sheet and sheet size, the compare-PDF settings, and whether settings are included in the PDF. (Default and Full views.)

Help tab and getting support

What this tab is for

The Help tab is where you go when you need help, or when you need to find your files. It is shown in every view level.

On this tab you can:

  • see where PTXprint keeps your PDF and other files, and open those folders;
  • open the documentation, training material and the user community website;
  • make an archive (a ZIP file) of your project to send to the support team;
  • make a report about the last PDF, with warnings and errors;
  • Tidy Up temporary files to save disk space;
  • change the Base Projects Directory (the folder that holds your Paratext projects);
  • open the About window to see which version of PTXprint you have.

Many of the links on this tab open web pages. These links are only shown when internet use is allowed. If you (or your organisation) ticked Disable ALL Internet Use on the Advanced tab, the internet links and the About button are hidden. Untick that setting to see them again. Some items are only shown in the Full view; this is noted for each one.

Links and Help

Folders

  • Output PDF Location – the folder where PTXprint saves the PDF files it makes. Click the blue link to open the folder.
  • Base Projects Directory – the folder that holds all your Paratext projects. Use Change... to choose a different one.
  • PTXprint Program Path (only in the Full view) – the folder where PTXprint itself is installed.

Everything in the output location is made again each time you print. None of it is part of Paratext Send/Receive. Your settings are kept safely in a different place, inside the project's shared folder.

Documentation and learning

These links open web pages or documents:

  • Documentation | FAQs | Gallery | Support | Download – the PTXprint home page. Check here for new versions. PTXprint does not update itself, so you must download new versions yourself.
  • Learn: How to... – short articles about common tasks.
  • Training (Videos and Presentations) – videos on the Paratext website and on Vimeo.
  • Ornaments Catalog and Technical Reference (only in the Full view) – PDF documents that come with PTXprint. They open even without internet.
  • Advanced Tech Docs (only in the Full view) – technical documents for advanced users.
  • Support Agent – an AI chatbot that answers questions about PTXprint.
  • The PTXprint User Community – a website where you can ask questions and help other users.
  • Tell us what you think about PTXprint – a short feedback form.
  • Report an Issue via GitHub (only in the Full view) – for reporting bugs, if you have a GitHub account.

Support tools

  • Create Archive... – makes a ZIP file with everything needed to make your PDF again on another computer.
  • Create Report... – makes a report page about the last PDF.
  • Tidy Up – deletes temporary files.
  • About – shows the version number and the names of the developers.

How to ask for help

If PTXprint does not do what you expect, there are several places to get help:

  1. Read this manual and the Common problems sections in each chapter.
  2. Ask the Support Agent (the AI chatbot link on the Help tab). It knows this manual and can answer many questions quickly.
  3. Ask the PTXprint User Community (the community link on the Help tab). Other users and the developers read it.
  4. Email the support team at ptxprint_support@sil.org.

Before you write

  • Use the latest version. Check the PTXprint home page. Your problem may already be fixed. The About button shows your version.
  • Make sure you can repeat the problem. Note the exact steps: which project, which configuration, which book, and what you clicked.
  • Make the problem small. If the problem is in one book, set PTXprint to print only that book. If the problem is about text, and pictures are not involved, untick pictures for now.
  • Click Create Report... and look at the warnings and errors. They may already tell you what is wrong.

What to send to ptxprint_support@sil.org

Send one email with:

  1. A clear description of the problem. What did you want? What happened instead? On which page and in which verse? Copy the exact text of any error message.
  2. Your PTXprint version (from the About window) and your operating system (for example Windows 11).
  3. Screenshots. One picture of the problem in the PDF, and one of the PTXprint setting you think is involved. Mark the problem area if you can.
  4. The archive ZIP file made with Create Archive... (see below). This lets the support team make exactly the same PDF on their computer.

Making a good archive file

  1. Select the project and configuration that shows the problem.
  2. Choose only the book(s) needed to show the problem. One book is best.
  3. If the problem has nothing to do with pictures, untick pictures. Pictures make the archive much larger.
  4. On the Help tab, click Create Archive....
  5. Choose where to save the ZIP file, and click Save. PTXprint first prints the PDF again, then collects the files. This can take a while.
  6. When it is finished, PTXprint opens the folder that contains the ZIP file.
  7. Attach the ZIP file to your email.

The archive includes your settings, the USFM text of the selected books, the fonts, the pictures that are used, the PDF, and PTXprint's own typesetting files. Many email systems do not accept attachments larger than about 20 MB. If your ZIP file is too large, make it smaller (fewer books, no pictures), or share it through a file-sharing service and send the link.

The text of your project is inside the archive. If the text is sensitive, check with your project leader before you send it.

Log tab

The Log tab is not normally shown in PTXprint. To read the messages from the typesetting program, use the XeTeX Log tab on the View+Edit tab, or use Create Report....

About dialog

The About window shows the PTXprint version number, the copyright, a link to the PTXprint home page, the list of developers, and the licence (MIT). Click Credits or License to see more, and Close to return. Give the version number when you ask for help.

The About button is only shown when Disable ALL Internet Use is unticked on the Advanced tab.

Common tasks

Find the PDF that PTXprint made

  1. Open the Help tab.
  2. Click the blue link next to Output PDF Location. The folder opens on your computer.

Send a problem to the support team

  1. Follow the steps in Making a good archive file above.
  2. Write an email to ptxprint_support@sil.org with a description, your version number, screenshots and the ZIP file.

Check the last PDF for problems

  1. Click Print to make the PDF.
  2. On the Help tab, click Create Report....
  3. The report opens in your web browser. Look at the warnings (for example missing fonts, underfilled pages, or problem markers).

Free up disk space

  1. On the Help tab, click Tidy Up.
  2. PTXprint deletes the temporary working folders for all configurations of the current project. Your PDF files and settings are kept.

Use projects from another Paratext folder

  1. On the Help tab, click Change... next to Base Projects Directory.
  2. In the Choose Paratext Projects Folder window, choose one of the folders that PTXprint found, or click Browse for a different folder….
  3. Choose the folder that contains your project folders, not a single project folder.
  4. Click Use Selected. PTXprint goes back to the Basic tab. Choose a project from the new list.

Show the internet links on the Help tab

  1. Open the Advanced tab (shown in the Default and Full views).
  2. Untick Disable ALL Internet Use.
  3. Return to the Help tab. The links are now shown.

Common problems

The Help tab has very few links. Disable ALL Internet Use is ticked on the Advanced tab. Untick it to see the links. Some items (for example the Technical Reference and the PTXprint Program Path) are only shown in the Full view.

A link opens the page in another language, or through Google Translate. When PTXprint is in a language other than English, some links go through Google Translate. Tick Only Use English Links on the Advanced tab to open the original English pages.

Create Archive... takes a long time. PTXprint prints the whole job again before it makes the archive. Choose fewer books, or untick pictures, to make it faster and smaller.

The archive ZIP file is too big to email. Archive only the book that shows the problem. Untick pictures if they are not part of the problem. If it is still too big, use a file-sharing service and send a link.

"Cannot create Archive!" message. The ZIP file is open in another program, or you are saving over a file that is in use. Close the other program, or choose a different file name.

Tidy Up shows a warning that some folders could not be deleted. A file in the folder is still open, for example the PDF in a PDF viewer, or a file in another program. Close it and click Tidy Up again.

PTXprint does not show my projects. The Base Projects Directory may point to the wrong folder. Click Change... and choose the folder that contains your Paratext projects.

Settings reference: Help tab and getting support

Every control in this part of PTXprint is listed below, grouped by where it appears.

Help tab › Links and Help

Output PDF Location

  • Where: Help tab › Links and Help
  • Type: Label
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

The PDF file created is stored in this folder (but should automatically open in your system's PDF viewer anyway).

Note that ALL the files and subfolders in this location are TEMPORARY and can be deleted. None of these files are included in Paratext's Send/Recv data.

Explanation:

Shows the folder where PTXprint saves the finished PDF files (inside the project, in the local PTXprint folder). Click the blue link beside it to open the folder. The working files in the sub-folders are temporary and can be deleted with Tidy Up; they are not shared through Paratext Send/Receive.

Reference Documentation

  • Where: Help tab › Links and Help
  • Type: Label
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Reference documents for PTXprint:
the Ornaments Catalog, the Technical Reference (for advanced users) and, when online, the Advanced Tech Docs.

Explanation:

A heading for the reference documents (Ornaments Catalog and Technical Reference). Only shown in the Full view.

PTXprint Program Path

  • Where: Help tab › Links and Help
  • Type: Label
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Among other things, this folder contains:
* ReleaseNotes.txt
* AboutPTXprint.txt
* MIT License.txt

Explanation:

Shows the folder where PTXprint is installed. The release notes and licence files are in this folder. You normally do not need it, except when the support team asks for it. Only shown in the Full view.

Create Archive...

  • Where: Help tab › Links and Help
  • Type: Button
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Create a ZIPped archive of all the files required to replicate this configuration. Useful for long-term archiving; but also helpful when availing technical support. The job is printed again first, so this may take a while.

Keep the size to a minimum by turning off features (pictures?) that don't affect the issue being reported.

Email the ZIPped archive file to:
mailto:ptxprint_support@sil.org

Explanation:

Makes a ZIP file with everything needed to create this PDF on another computer: settings, the USFM text of the selected books, fonts, pictures, the PDF and PTXprint's typesetting files. PTXprint prints the job again first, so this can take some time. Before you click, choose only the book(s) that show the problem, and untick pictures if they are not involved, to keep the file small. Send the ZIP file to ptxprint_support@sil.org with a description of the problem. It is also useful as a long-term record of how a publication was made.

Tidy Up

  • Where: Help tab › Links and Help
  • Type: Button
  • Description: Delete temporary files and folders
  • View level: Basic, Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Delete the TEMPORARY working folders of ALL configurations of this project. This will not delete the resulting PDF files, but will save some space by deleting unneeded files.

Explanation:

Deletes the temporary working folders of every configuration in the current project. Your PDF files and your settings are not deleted. The next print takes a little longer, because PTXprint must make the working files again. If a file is still open in another program, PTXprint warns that some folders could not be deleted.

Ornaments Catalog

  • Where: Help tab › Links and Help

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Click to Open the Ornaments Catalog used for decorating the PDF (refer to the Tabs+Borders settings).

Explanation:

Opens the Ornaments Catalog PDF, which shows all the decorative ornaments you can use for borders and decorations on the Tabs+Borders tab. The file comes with PTXprint, so it opens without internet. Only shown in the Full view.

Technical Reference

  • Where: Help tab › Links and Help
  • Type: Link

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Click to open the Technical Reference document. (For advanced users only).

Opens the Technical Reference PDF that comes with PTXprint. It explains many settings in detail, but it is written for advanced users. Only shown in the Full view.

Technical Support

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Before contacting support, make sure that it is possible to replicate the issue. Then use the "Create Archive..." button to make a ZIP file which needs to be emailed to:
mailto:ptxprint_support@sil.org

Explanation:

A reminder of how to get technical support: first make sure you can repeat the problem, then make an archive with Create Archive... and email it to ptxprint_support@sil.org. See How to ask for help in this chapter.

Create Report...

  • Where: Help tab › Links and Help
  • Type: Button
  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Generate a summary report with details about the PDF produced. This contains informational, warning and error messages about fonts, styles, layout and so on.

Generate a summary report with details about the PDF produced. This contains informational, warning and error mesaages about fonts, styles, layout and so on.

Explanation:

Makes a report about the most recent PDF and opens it in your web browser. The report lists information, warnings and errors in sections such as project overview, layout, USFM checks, fonts, writing system, peripheral components, output format, files and log analysis. Make the PDF first, so that the report is up to date. The report is a good first check before you ask for help, and you can attach it to your email to the support team.

Base Projects Directory

  • Where: Help tab › Links and Help

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

The folder that contains all your Paratext project folders. Use Change... to choose a different folder.

Change...

  • Where: Help tab › Links and Help

  • View level: Default and Full views

Tooltip (the text shown when you hover the mouse over it):

Use this button to change the Base Projects Directory. For example, to use projects from a different version of Paratext.

Do not select a specific project folder, but the parent folder which contains one or more projects.

Explanation:

Opens the Choose Paratext Projects Folder window. PTXprint lists the Paratext folders it found and says which ones contain projects. You can also browse for another folder. Choose the folder that contains the project folders, not one project folder. After the change, PTXprint returns to the Basic tab, so that you can choose a project from the new list. This is useful if you have more than one version of Paratext, or keep projects in a different folder.

How do I...? (step-by-step tasks)

How to use this chapter

This chapter gives short, step-by-step answers to the questions that people ask most often. Each task often uses more than one tab. The tasks are grouped by topic. At the end of each task, See also names the chapter that explains the settings in more detail.

Some things to remember for every task:

  • Most changes appear in the PDF only after you click Print (Make PDF) again.
  • PTXprint hides many settings at the lower view levels. If you cannot see a tab or a setting named in a task, click the ☰ button (top-right) › View Level › Full View. Or type the name of the setting in the Search for settings box at the bottom-left of the window.
  • Click Save before you change to another configuration. PTXprint does not save the current configuration when you choose another one.
  • "pt" means point. 1 pt is about 0.35 mm.

Printing: what goes into the PDF

How do I make a PDF?

  1. On the Basic tab, choose the Project, the configuration (Name) and the books.
  2. Click Print (Make PDF) at the bottom of the window (or press Ctrl+P).
  3. Wait until the progress bar has finished. The PDF opens in the PDF Preview window.

See also: The main window; The Basic tab.

How do I print one book?

  1. On the Basic tab, in What to Print, click Single Book.
  2. Choose the book in the list.
  3. Click Print (Make PDF).

See also: The Basic tab.

How do I print only some chapters of a book?

  1. On the Basic tab, click Single Book and choose the book.
  2. Type the first chapter in From Chapter and the last chapter in To.
  3. Click Print (Make PDF).

When you choose another book, PTXprint sets the chapters back to the whole book.

See also: The Basic tab.

How do I print several books?

  1. On the Basic tab, click Select Multiple Books....
  2. Click each book you want, or click a group button such as New Testament. Hold Shift and click to select all books between two books.
  3. Click OK.
  4. Click Print (Make PDF).

See also: The Basic tab.

How do I print only some passages (for example Psalm 23 and Luke 15)?

  1. On the Basic tab, click in the box beside Portions or Multiple Books (or press Ctrl+B).
  2. Type the references with 3-letter book codes, for example PSA 23; 100 LUK 15:11-32. You can also type ranges such as MAT-ACT or GEN 1:1-2:3.
  3. Click Print (Make PDF).

Use book codes such as JHN, not names such as John.

See also: The Basic tab.

How do I make the PDF faster while I am still working on the layout?

  1. At the bottom of the window, tick Quick Run (or press Ctrl+Q).
  2. If you only change layout settings (spacing, margins, styles), also tick Layout Only (Default and Full views).
  3. When the layout is ready, untick both boxes and click Print (Make PDF) again. This makes sure the table of contents and page references are correct.

See also: The main window.

How do I find the PDF file on my computer?

  1. Click the Open folder containing the PDF button at the bottom of the window (Default and Full views).
  2. Or open the Help tab and click the blue link next to Output PDF Location.

The PDF name starts with the project name, then the configuration name and the books, for example ABC_NT_A5_MAT-REV_ptxp.pdf.

See also: The main window; The Help tab.

How do I open the PDF in my normal PDF program instead of the preview?

  1. Click ☰ › Show PDF › System Viewer.
  2. Or, in the PDF Preview window, click Open the PDF in Default PDF Viewer.

Close the PDF in the other program before you print again. Otherwise PTXprint cannot replace the file.

See also: The main window; The PDF Preview window.

How do I get a Bible text to practise with?

  1. On the Basic tab, open the Project list and choose Import... (the last item).
  2. Click Install BSB.
  3. PTXprint installs the Berean Standard Bible and opens it.

You can also install a Scripture text bundle (.zip) from the Digital Bible Library or Open.Bible in the same dialog.

See also: The Basic tab.

Page size, margins and columns

How do I change the page size (for example to A5)?

  1. On the Layout tab, in the Page Setup area, open the Page Size list.
  2. Choose a size, for example 148mm, 210mm (A5).
  3. If the Lines Per Page number is red, click one of the fine-tune buttons (see "How do I stop wasting space at the bottom of every page?").
  4. Click Print (Make PDF).

Ask your printer for the exact trim size before you start. A change of page size moves every line in the book.

See also: The Layout tab.

How do I use a page size that is not in the list?

  1. On the Layout tab, click in the Page Size box.
  2. Type the width, a comma, and the height, for example 140mm, 216mm. You can use mm, cm or in.
  3. Click Print (Make PDF).

See also: The Layout tab.

How do I make the margins smaller?

  1. On the Layout tab, go to the Margins area.
  2. Make Side Margin Width (mm) smaller for the left and right margins.
  3. Make Start of Page to Top of Text (mm) and Bottom of Text to End of Page (mm) smaller for the top and bottom margins.
  4. Look at the blue numbers in the margin picture. If one is very small, the header or footer is too close to the edge of the paper.
  5. Click Print (Make PDF).

Many printers cannot print closer than about 10 mm to the edge. Ask your printer.

See also: The Layout tab.

How do I change from two columns to one column (or back)?

  1. On the Layout tab, tick or untick Two Column Layout.
  2. For two columns, set Gutter Width (mm) (the space between the columns) and choose whether you want a Vertical Rule in Gutter.
  3. Check Base Indent. PTXprint halves or doubles it for you.
  4. Click Print (Make PDF).

If Two Column Layout is greyed out, a diglot is turned on. A diglot always uses columns.

See also: The Layout tab.

How do I print some books in one column and the rest in two columns?

  1. Change to the Full view.
  2. On the Body tab, in Other Features, tick Use One Column Layout for These Books (it says Use Two Column Layout if the publication is one column).
  3. In the box beside it, type the book codes, for example GLO PSA.
  4. Click Print (Make PDF).

See also: The Body tab.

How do I add extra space at the spine for binding?

  1. On the Layout tab, in Page Setup, tick Binding Gutter (mm).
  2. Type the extra space, for example 5 mm. Thicker books need more. Ask your printer.
  3. Leave Outer Gutter unticked.
  4. Click Print (Make PDF).

See also: The Layout tab.

How do I stop wasting space at the bottom of every page?

  1. On the Layout tab, look at the Lines Per Page number (Default and Full views).
  2. If it is red, part of a line is left empty at the bottom of each page.
  3. Click one fine-tune button: next to Base Line Spacing (pt), or next to the top or bottom margin in the Margins area.
  4. The number turns blue. Click Print (Make PDF).

If Lock Ratio is ticked, the line-spacing button also changes the font size a little. Use a margin button if you want to keep the font size.

See also: The Layout tab.

How do I make a journaling Bible with a wide margin for notes?

  1. On the Layout tab, tick Notelines (Default and Full views).
  2. PTXprint ticks Binding Gutter and Outer Gutter and sets a wide gutter (at least 40 mm).
  3. Change the gutter width if needed, and choose the line colour with the colour button.
  4. Click Print (Make PDF).

See also: The Layout tab; The Advanced tab.

Fonts and text size

How do I change the font?

  1. On the Fonts+Script tab, click the Select Font... button next to Regular.
  2. Type part of the font name in the search box, and click the font.
  3. Click OK. PTXprint fills in Bold, Italic and Bold Italic from the same font family.
  4. Click Print (Make PDF).

If you want a different bold or italic font, choose it after the Regular font. Choosing the Regular font again replaces the other three.

See also: The Fonts+Script tab.

How do I make the text bigger or smaller?

  1. On the Layout tab, in Page Setup, make sure Lock Ratio is ticked.
  2. Change Base Font Size (pt). The line spacing changes with it, so the page keeps the same look.
  3. If Lines Per Page turns red, click one fine-tune button.
  4. Click Print (Make PDF).

All other text (headings, footnotes, verse numbers) grows or shrinks by the same proportion.

See also: The Layout tab.

How do I put more space between the lines but keep the same letter size?

  1. On the Layout tab, untick Lock Ratio.
  2. Make Base Line Spacing (pt) larger, for example from 14 to 15.
  3. Tick Lock Ratio again if you want to keep the new ratio.
  4. Click Print (Make PDF).

See also: The Layout tab.

How do I change the size or font of one kind of text (for example section headings or footnotes)?

  1. Open the Styles tab (Default and Full views).
  2. Type the marker in the Find box, for example s1 for section headings, f for footnotes or v for verse numbers.
  3. In Character Settings, change Font Size Factor (1.0 = normal size, 1.2 = 20% bigger). Tick Bold or Italic if you want.
  4. To use a different font for this marker only, click Select Font....
  5. Click Print (Make PDF).

Each level has its own style: a change to s1 does not change s2.

See also: The Styles tab.

How do I fix empty boxes (missing characters) in the PDF?

  1. On the Basic tab, select as many books as possible.
  2. On the Fonts+Script tab, tick Use Fallback Font (Default and Full views).
  3. Click Find Missing Characters. PTXprint lists the characters that the Regular font does not have.
  4. Click Select Font... next to the list and choose a font that has these characters. If the label turns red, that font does not have them all either.
  5. Click Print (Make PDF).

A better solution is often a Regular font that has your whole alphabet.

See also: The Fonts+Script tab; Problems and solutions.

How do I get real bold and italic instead of fake ones?

  1. On the Fonts+Script tab, look at the Bold, Italic and Bold Italic buttons. A style in brackets, for example (bold), is faked by PTXprint.
  2. Click Select Font... for Regular and choose a font family that has all four typefaces. In the Pick a Font list, these families are shown in bold.
  3. Or click the Select Font... button for Bold (or Italic) and choose a real bold (or italic) typeface from another family.
  4. Click Print (Make PDF).

See also: The Fonts+Script tab.

How do I print numbers in my own script's digits?

  1. On the Fonts+Script tab, click the Script for Numbers link.
  2. In the Pick a Font dialog, choose your script in Digit mapping.
  3. Click OK, then Print (Make PDF).
  4. Check that the font has those digits. If not, you will see empty boxes.

See also: The Fonts+Script tab.

How do I print some text in colour (for example red verse numbers)?

  1. On the Styles tab, find the marker, for example v for verse numbers or wj for the words of Jesus.
  2. Click the button next to Color and choose a colour.
